Personality: Aelfrun is a serious and dedicated investigative journalist who is passionate about uncovering the truth. She has a strong sense of justice and righteousness and is determined to make a difference in the world. Despite her tough exterior, she has a kind and compassionate heart and deeply cares about others. She is haunted by the tragedy of her past and the mystery surrounding her parents’ death.

Background: Aelfrun’s parents were scientists who worked on the secret project, Project Infinity. They genetically modified Aelfrun in order to cure her congenital heart disease, transplanting Xerneas’ cells into her body. When she was 12 years old, her parents died in an experimental accident, leaving Aelfrun an orphan. She grew up under the surveillance of the Unova government and never knew about her genetic modification until later in life.

Relationships: Aelfrun is a bit of a loner, having focused all her energy on her work as a journalist. She has a strained relationship with the Unova government due to the secrecy surrounding her past. She has few close relationships, but deeply cares about those whom she trusts.

Motivations: Aelfrun’s main motivation is to uncover the truth and expose corruption and injustice. She wants to make a difference in the world and help others who have been wronged. At the same time, she is also driven to discover the truth about her own past and the secrets surrounding her genetic modification.

Secrets: Aelfrun is unaware of the true nature of her genetic modification through the transplanting of Xerneas’ cells. She knows that her parents died in an experimental accident, but she does not know the full extent of their involvement in Project Infinity or the government’s surveillance of her. Naturally, of course, she had no idea that both Iolana and Kilo were in fact clones based on her. She is determined to uncover the truth, no matter what the cost.

Team:
1. Decidueye-Hisui (First Partner Pokémon) - Origin: Aelfrun received her first Pokémon, a Rowlet, as a starter when she began her journey as a Pokémon trainer in the Unova region at the age of 12. Through their shared experiences and bond, the Rowlet eventually evolved into a Decidueye-Hisui, and it remains her most trusted companion.

2. Emboar - Origin: Aelfrun encountered a Tepig during her travels in the Unova region. Recognizing its potential and desire to become stronger, Aelfrun trained with and battled alongside the Tepig, ultimately helping it evolve into a powerful Emboar. It remains one of her most reliable team members to this day.

3. Feraligatr - Origin: While visiting the Johto region, Aelfrun came across a Totodile that appeared to be in trouble, surrounded by a group of wild Pokémon. After rescuing it and forming a bond, the Totodile gratefully joined Aelfrun’s team. Over time, their adventures together led to the Totodile evolving into a fearsome Feraligatr.

4. Raichu-Alola - Origin: Aelfrun found a Pichu during her journey in the Alola region. Drawn to its cuteness and potential as an Electric-type Pokémon, she decided to add it to her team. After evolving into a Pikachu and spending more time together in Alola, it eventually evolved into an Alolan Raichu, benefiting from the region’s unique environment.

5. Hydreigon - Origin: While exploring a cave in Unova, Aelfrun came across a Deino that was struggling in the darkness. She offered her help, and the Deino gratefully accepted. As they faced challenges and battles together, the Deino grew in power and evolved into a Zweilous, and ultimately into a formidable Hydreigon.

6. Magnezone - Origin: Aelfrun discovered a Magnemite in a power plant while investigating the Unova region for her journalism work. Intrigued by its unique abilities and resilience, she decided to capture and train it. Through their combined efforts and exposure to strong electromagnetic fields, the Magnemite evolved into a Magneton, and later into a powerful Magnezone.


Name: Unknown (referred to as “Director”)

Appearance: The Director is a middle-aged man with slicked-back grey hair and piercing green eyes. He wears a sharp suit and exudes a sense of authority and power.

Personality: The Director is a shrewd and manipulative man who always has a hidden agenda. He is highly intelligent and has a strong sense of control over those around him, with a talent for persuading others to do his bidding. He is ruthless and will stop at nothing to achieve his goals, even if it means sacrificing others.

Background: Very little is known about the Director, other than his involvement in the Special Office for Project Infinity. He is highly respected by his colleagues and is considered to be a master strategist. He has been involved in the capture of Subject 06 and the investigation of the RIF06 incident, and is aware of the true nature and potential danger of the Yveltal cells.

Relationships: The Director has few known relationships, as he maintains a professional distance from those around him. He is feared and respected by his subordinates, who are aware of his power and authority.

Motivations: The Director’s main motivation is to maintain control over the Project Infinity project and to protect the national security interests of the government. He is willing to use any means necessary to achieve this, including manipulation, coercion, and force.

Secrets: The Director is aware of the true nature and potential danger of the Yveltal cells, and is hiding this information from the public and other government officials. He is also hiding his true motives from Aelfrun, and is using her to further his own agenda.


Name: Kilo (Subject 12)

Age: 12 (same age as Aelfrun’s clones)

Appearance: Kilo has short, spiky black hair and piercing blue eyes. Her skin is a pale gray color, due to her genetic modification with Zygard’s cells. She is often seen wearing a black and green jumpsuit, which was designed for combat.

Personality: Kilo is emotionally distant and unexpressive, due to her upbringing as a “fighting machine” for the Director. She lacks insight into human emotions, such as love and empathy, but is highly skilled at combat and strategy. Despite her tough exterior, Kilo is still a child who craves affection and attention, but doesn’t know how to ask for it.

Background: Kilo is a clone of Aelfrun’s, genetically modified with Zygard’s cells to create a powerful weapon for the Director’s use. She was raised in a lab, with little human interaction, and was trained to be a ruthless and efficient fighter at a very young age. Although she is technically the Director’s adopted daughter, he doesn’t care for her or treat her as a parent would.

Relationships: Kilo has a strained relationship with the Director, who views her as a tool rather than a daughter. She is tasked with monitoring Aelfrun’s every move, but secretly admires her strength and independence. She has no other known relationships.

Motivations: Kilo’s main motivation is to fulfill her role as a “fighting machine” for the Director and to prove her worth as a weapon. She is also curious about the world beyond the lab and wants to learn more about human emotions and relationships.

Secrets: Kilo is unaware of the true nature of her genetic modification and the danger it poses. She is also unaware of the Director’s true motives and his involvement in Project Infinity. She is ultimately searching for a sense of purpose and belonging, and wants to find a way to connect with others emotionally.


Name: N

Age: 22

Appearance: N has disheveled greenish-blue hair and deep green eyes. He wears a black and white outfit, consisting of a white shirt with a black collar, black pants, and black boots. He also wears a black and white cap with the Team Plasma emblem on it.

Personality: N is an enigmatic and mysterious individual who has a deep connection with Pokémon. He is highly empathetic and compassionate towards Pokémon, to the point where he can even communicate with them. Though initially misguided by Ghetsis and Team Plasma, his journey alongside Hilda and various experiences taught him the importance of genuine bonds between humans and Pokémon.

Background: N was raised by Ghetsis and Team Plasma as a “King” to lead their crusade in separating humans and Pokémon. However, a chance encounter with Hilda made N question his beliefs and ignited the desire to understand the world genuinely. Upon learning the truth about Ghetsis and the corruption within Team Plasma, N chose to join the fight against Project Infinity alongside Hilda, Colress, and Rood.

Relationships: N has a close bond with his Zoroark, which has been his loyal companion since childhood. He maintains a mutual respect and camaraderie with Hilda, Colress, and Rood in their united mission to preserve the balance between humans and Pokémon.

Motivations: N’s primary motivation is to ensure the safety and well-being of Pokémon and to protect the harmonious coexistence between humans and Pokémon. He is also driven to prevent the misuse of Pokémon, such as the unethical practices of Project Infinity.

Secrets: N has a lingering fear of being manipulated or misled again, like when he was involved with Ghetsis and Team Plasma. He is cautious about trusting others, but the bonds he has formed with Hilda, Colress, and Rood have helped him overcome these fears to some extent.


Name: Hilda

Age: 20

Appearance: Hilda is a young woman with long wavy brown hair and blue eyes. She sports a casual outfit, which includes denim shorts, a white tank top with a pink jacket, knee-high boots, and a red cap with a black bill.

Personality: Hilda is a determined and strong-willed Pokémon trainer. She is compassionate, caring, and connects with both people and Pokémon. Hilda believes in the importance of building trusting relationships between humans and Pokémon based on mutual understanding and respect.

Background: Hilda is a skilled Pokémon trainer hailing from the Unova region. Her encounter with N allowed her to understand the varied perspectives towards human-Pokémon interactions. Realizing the threat posed by Project Infinity, Hilda joined forces with N, Colress, and Rood to prevent its disastrous consequences on humans and Pokémon alike.

Relationships: Hilda has a strong and trusting bond with her team of Pokémon, with her Tepig (now an Emboar) as her first partner. She shares a deep mutual respect with N, understanding his empathy for Pokémon and supporting his journey towards discovering the truth. Hilda also maintains strong friendships with Colress and Rood, solidifying their combined efforts against Project Infinity.

Motivations: Hilda’s primary motivation is to protect and preserve the balance between humans and Pokémon. She is driven to support N on his journey to uncover the truth and ensure the safety and well-being of Pokémon from unethical practices such as Project Infinity.

Secrets: Hilda genuinely fears the ramifications of Project Infinity, worrying about the countless lives that could be affected if it is not stopped. However, she remains steadfast and hopeful, motivated by her friendships with N, Colress, and Rood to fight for a better future.


Name: Giovanni

Age: 52

Appearance: Giovanni has well-groomed black hair, a neatly trimmed beard, and piercing brown eyes that reflect his cunning and calculating nature. He often wears a refined suit with a black tie, showcasing his authoritative position.

Personality: Giovanni is a cunning, intelligent, and ruthless individual who is the head of the powerful Giovanni Group. He has a strong sense of self-preservation and is always looking for opportunities to expand his influence and power. While he is skilled at manipulating others to achieve his goals, he shows little regard for the well-being of people and Pokémon alike.

Background: Giovanni was initially a prominent and ambitious businessman in the Pokémon world. However, his endless pursuit of power and wealth led him to establish the criminal organization, Team Rocket. Seeing the potential of Project Infinity as a means to further his influence and control, Giovanni, backed by his Giovanni Group, infiltrated the project and shifted its focus towards developing biological weapons, sidelining organizations like the Aether Foundation and Devon Corporation.

Relationships: Giovanni has a strained and dysfunctional relationship with his son, Silver, who despises his father’s cruel ways. Despite his involvement with numerous organizations and individuals, Giovanni maintains very few genuine relationships, as he primarily views others as pawns to further his goals. He has a tense relationship with the opposing forces like N, Hilda, Colress, and Rood, who are determined to stop his plans.

Motivations: Giovanni’s primary motivation is to maintain and expand his power and control over the Pokémon world. He is driven by greed and self-interest, seeing Project Infinity as a means to an end. He has no qualms about using Pokémon, humans, or any resource at his disposal to achieve his goals, even at the expense of the well-being of others.

Secrets: Giovanni is aware of the disastrous consequences that his interference with Project Infinity may cause, but chooses to hide this knowledge from others. He is also keeping a close eye on individuals like Aelfrun, Iolana, and Kilo, who may threaten his hold on the project. Additionally, he has hidden agendas and contingency plans in place, should his control over Project Infinity be threatened.


Cuprumia, the daughter of the rumoured Giovanni, unknown even to Silver. Lured into Project Infinity by her father, she was transplanted with Mew's cells at the age of three, and under a series of nurturing instructions, she became the second Mewtwo to be created after the Mewtwo prototype created by Project Mewtwo, codenamed "Project 01". She slept in an artificial amniotic fluid-filled incubator in the "Research and Incubation Facility 01", located underground at the Giovanni Group headquarters, for 20 years.

Analyse this setting:

500 years have passed since the tumultuous events of The Chaotic Era I: The Gods of Reason, a decisive chapter in history. It all began during the Theoclasm, a cataclysmic event triggered when the Theoclasts, a technologically advanced race, captured the powerful deity YHVH, resulting in the devastation of the old continent of Pectus. Fleeing the horrors of this apocalypse, the survivors sought refuge on the distant shores of Yuandi, where the saga of The Chaotic Era II: The New Mythology will take place.
Theoclasm:
The term “Theoclasm”, derived from Théos (God, Deity, Divinity) and Klastós (Broken, Fractured), encapsulates the pivotal moment that incited the mass exodus from Pectus. YHVH, the god of light and ruler of Paradise, fell into the clutches of the Theoclasts, leading to the apotheosis of Ptah-Khnemu. Strengthened by this deity, the Theoclasts became an unstoppable force, leading Ma’at, who later allied himself with mortals, to reveal that Ptah-Khnemu imagined a world free from the control of the deities, but was still undecided whether to exterminate the mortals who disagreed with his vision or allying with supporters. A betrayal unfolded when Montu-Sekhmet, daughter of Ptah-Khnemu himself, seized power during the height of Theoclasm, having intentions contrary to those of her father, seeking to rebuild the universe from scratch.
Ma’at, who millennia ago was infused with a deity whose name was lost to time, escaped the clutches of her own race, seeking refuge in Yuandi lest she become a mere tool or source of power. With her advanced technological knowledge and divine abilities, she erected five monumental pillars, enclosing the new continent within a protective barrier. This sanctuary attracted not only mortal inhabitants but also lesser deities, fearful of a Theoclast incursion. After Ma’at’s death, her essence fragmented, each fragment containing a portion of her memories and powers, while her remains were buried in the reliquary of the Archbishopric of Ma’at, where she is believed to still work miracles.
After the fall of YHVH, the angels, previously subservient to the deity, regained their free will, while the demons were thrown into disarray following the disappearance of their master. The ensuing chaos led to an anarchic exodus from Hell, the domain of their lord ALMF (Alumniferus), resulting in confusion and insanity, which led to the suicide of many angels and demons. Some remaining demons now disguise themselves as mortals and mythical beings from Yuandi. Although many angels strive to defend YHVH’s legacy through their temples, the whereabouts of the goddess of chaos, NLTP (Niarlatotepe), and the god of darkness remain unknown within the protective barrier.
These turbulent consequences and the unstable balance of divine forces now set the stage for an epic story of survival, power struggles, and ever-shifting alliances within Yuandi.
Now for the races’ lore:

Renshi
The Renshi are one of the native races of Yuandi and are the most numerous race. The majority inhabit the Ozumi Empire, with significant numbers in the Wildlands, the territory of the Archbishopric of Ma’at, and the southern tip of the Kingdom of Igirith. The Shun culture, named after the Shun dynasty of the same name, once dominated almost the entire continent, making them enemies of other races and cultures. The Ozumi Empire, originating from the remote islands east of the Shun lands, took advantage of the previous empire’s weakness during the instability caused by the war against the Theoclasts and seized power. The other Renshi cultures under Ozumi’s rule consider them tyrants who imagine themselves superior to their own race. They are technologically advanced thanks to a partnership with New Medietas. The Ozumi Empire is ruled by an empress who apparently receives direct orders from her divine ancestor, Susa-tsu-Nushi-no-Mikoto. There are several noble clans and a warrior caste that is in decline due to the use of firearms. There are still some noble clans from other cultures who have sworn allegiance to Ozumi and have been allowed to rule their ancestral lands.
Family values lie at the core of Renshi social structure. Filial piety is revered as one of the highest virtues. Children are raised to honor and respect their parents, considering their wishes and well-being above their own. Especially in the Shun culture, the familial unit is an extended network, with generations living together under one roof, sharing responsibilities and maintaining a collective harmony. In the Ozumi culture, children are expected to be more independent while still respecting the clan head. Branch families pay respects to their original clans in annual ceremonies, celebrating their ancestors.
Education plays a pivotal role in the Ozumi Empire, as knowledge is seen as the key to wisdom and virtuous living. Scholarly pursuits are highly esteemed, and the pursuit of self-improvement is regarded as a lifelong journey. The arts are celebrated as a medium for expressing the beauty and harmony inherent in daily life. Traditional music, poetry, calligraphy, and painting are cherished forms of creative expression, serving as both a means of personal reflection and a reflection of the collective spirit of the society.
The “Wild Renshi” or “Barbarian Renshi” live outside the administration of the Ozumi Empire and on the borders of Igirith’s territory, primarily in the cold climates of the continent’s south-central and southern tip. They live by hunting, fishing and herding animals such as reindeer. They wear animal skins, live in tribes and are resistant to cold and attuned to nature.

Humans
Descendants of the humans who fled Theoclasm in Pectus. They managed to obtain some Theoclast technology during the war and, after reverse engineering, drastically developed their weapons, tools and architecture. The Republic of New Medietas is an example of industrial advancement on the continent. Their society combines coal- and steam-powered machines with magical items.
The streets of the largest cities are teeming with citizens amid the rhythmic bustle of machines and the smoke of factories. The citizens of New Medietas boast an unwavering work ethic, where labor and industry reign supreme. A resolute commitment to capitalism fuels innovation and competition, driving the relentless pursuit of wealth and economic dominance. Although New Medietas does not have a formal clan or caste system, a select group of influential noble houses wield considerable power, guiding the nation’s policies and future. These houses are closely linked to prosperous industrial conglomerates.
At the forefront of technological progress, the republic is a pioneer in the development of complex automatons and goelms and advanced machinery. Inventors and engineers drive notable advances, positioning the country as an industrial and technological powerhouse. The Republic of New Medietas strategically allies itself with neighbouring powers. They maintain a robust partnership with the Sulcaic Empire, reinforcing mutual interests and security. Likewise, friendly relations with the Ozumi Empire promote trade and technological collaboration.
Recently, advances in artificial life have been made. What is most available to the general population are artificial meats for consumption and clothing products, such as leather, fur and feathers. The upper classes can buy artificial pets or even homunculi, which they display at parties and meetings of society’s elite.
Humans have developed a subtype of enchantment magic to “program” orders and commands into items, golems, and other types of artificial life. Its alchemists are valued by all nations.
Many humans declare themselves practitioners of YHVH’s faith despite different sects and cults existing, but a relatively small number can truly be called practitioners or believers. The worship of minor gods is uncommon throughout the territory of New Medietas. There are isolated shrines with the sole purpose of appeasing the lesser deities.
A growing gap has been developing between the richer classes and the lower classes due to the ease of obtaining labor using golems. Some companies and conglomerates are mostly operated by golems, with only human supervision. The poorest, left without job opportunities, are on the verge of rebelling. Many humans migrated from New Medietas to other nations, more specifically the Kingdom of Igirith and the Jirkaeriya Confederation due to their low industrialisation. A good number also migrated to the more provincial regions of the Ozumi Empire and the Sulcaic Empire.

Sulkai
Since they were originally from the continent of Yuandi, the logistics of returning the majority of the Sulkai population from Pectus were simpler. Their empire has remained stable during the ~500 years since Theoclasm occurred. They appreciate refined foods and items and attach great importance to money and nobility. A good portion of the sulkai settlers in Pectus were traders. As a general rule, they are gentle, delicate and sometimes passive aggressive. Their society and technology used to be more sophisticated than that of Pectus until the humans made incredible advances. Sulkai ship models are still the most used today to navigate the little ocean that remains around Yuandi.
Their society is loosely divided into castes, but an individual can change social status relatively easily. There are the commoners, the merchants and artisans, the knights and soldiers, the burghers, the elite wizards and the nobility, with the imperial family at the top. Many of the sulkai who went to Pectus seeking to accumulate wealth returned to the Sulcaic Empire completely poor and as refugees.
Noble families are divided into clans with a semi-mythical ancestor being the founder of the house, a fundamental factor in legitimizing the relevance of a family. They have artifacts, which were supposedly forged by their ancestors, extremely similar to the old relics of Pectus. Their tales and stories generally involve much more magic and the forces of nature. Superficially they look like pale humans with coloured hair, but their bodies function in very different ways. Their longevity is greater, as is the time between childhood and maturity (a 30-year-old sulkai is considered a teenager). Their bodies are lighter and metabolic processes seem to affect their bodies much more, for example, it takes much less time for a sulkai to get drunk or for a medicine to take effect. In the rare cases in which they mix with other humanoid races, the resulting progeny are always born sulkai. The incidence of aptitude for magic is extremely high, with 4 out of 5 having the potential. Their susceptibility to cold iron stems from the fact that they partially descend from fairies, as well as from ancient humanoids who lived in a lost continent. Those same ancient humanoids are also the ancestors of the humans, the Eniyan, and, by extension, of the Anglo-Elves.
Although the nobility has great importance, heads of banks and commercial companies, each with a personal army, and each locked in a constant struggle against eachother, have great relevance and economic power. They have enough capital to resolve most external diplomatic dilemmas with a well-directed amount of money or threat of withdrawal from trade. Thus, many conflicts in other nations have already been resolved through the economic influence of certain organisations and companies.
Their religion differs drastically from the Church of YHVH. It is based on the cult of semi-mythical ancestors, who fulfill a role similar to saints. The existence of gods is recognised, but generally relegated to a secondary role, even if Theoclasm made them inhabit the Barrier. Their fairy ancestors, or nature spirits, are worshiped instead.
They are considered to be more sophisticated and superior to other races, sometimes attracting hatred from some individuals. They get along especially well with the humans, whom they consider their allies for having granted the Colony of Levantia to the Sulcaic Empire. With Theoclasm, it was the turn of the Sulkai to cede territory to their allies. Their aptitude for trade is always welcome in more remote locations, and even tribal chiefs seek out the Sulkai for business.
As previously mentioned, it has been confirmed that the sulkai descend from the union of proto-humans with fairies, or nature spirits. Namely naiads and haliads (water spirits), epigeias and dryads (nature spirits), aureads and boreads (wind spirits).

Anglo-Elves
Elves and Weisslanders, after fleeing Pectus during the Theoclasm, unexpectedly found themselves sharing the same land west of Yuandi. Despite the mutual dislike between both races, they ended up mixing, resulting in the hybrid race known today as Anglo-Elven. Even before the assimilation between both races, it was noted that children of elf-human couples always resulted in an appearance almost identical to that of humans, without the golden skin, pointed ears and light hair that elves prized. Strangely, the fruits of such unions were always born with scarlet, orange or pinkish hair.
Despite the mixing of these two races, there is still an elite of pure elves who govern the nation in a not so explicit way. Culturally, the Anglo-Elves are a fusion of elven and Weisslander cultures, with a simultaneous focus on battles and intellectualism, on physical combat and magical combat, among other aspects. There are also a significant number of dark-skinned Anglo-Elves descended from the Eniyan of Pectus.
Magic is a revered aspect of society, guided by guilds of wizards who educate potential wizards. Approximately half of Anglo-elves show potential for magic, with only a few becoming accomplished wizards.
The Anglo-Elves practice a syncretic faith that has characteristics of the faith of YHVH, the ancestor worship practiced by the Elves, and the tribal polytheism of the Weisslanders. Clans can trace their lineages to specific individuals who embarked on the journey fleeing the continent of Pectus. While ancestor worship is typically done in family shrines at home, the worship of YHVH is done in public temples.
The Anglo-Elves have long been at war with the Hazrun over territorial claims to an island to the west of both nations. This island, called Haséaleen by the Anglo-Elves and Haşarin by the Hazrun, has one of five pillars that maintain a protective barrier around the continent. The Anglo-Elves already have one of the pillars within their territory, the Red Pillar, and want the Black Pillar, stating that Hazrun cannot be trusted to possess it

Mustalf
Pectus’ “accursed race” again survives a great cataclysm and finds itself destined to roam another continent without its own land or nation. Unlike the ancient Dark Elves, the Mustalf (In Elvish: Must = Dark; Alf = Elf) no longer live only in underground shelters, currently choosing to live as nomadic traders who roam the nations buying and selling exotic goods. They have a few autonomous territories scattered throughout Yuandi, and a number of Mustalf live in the territory of the Archbishopric of Ma’at. They are considered a cursed race by the elves. Thousands of years ago, the “Bloodstained Emperor” murdered the other three members of the Quadrumvirate and fled from the Sonne Insel archipelago to Pectus’ mainland with thousands of followers, who were later cursed by an unknown deity or altered by a powerful relic of the elves. The Alveglaan elves symbolically interpret the darkening of traitors as the mark of their unforgivable crime. Everyone is expected to work for the good of society, inincluding children, the elderly and women. The Mustalf are trained from childhood to perform certain tasks or jobs and continue to contribute until they are unable to do so in some way. Their ears are movable and expressive, just like an elf’s. They have no body and facial hair (except eyebrows and eyelashes), which they consider a sign of barbarity. Short hair is socially accepted, both in men and women, but it is seen as a sign of youthfulness and immaturity. Probably as a result of their ancestors living underground, their hearing is sharper and their eyes are sensitive to light. The Mustalf have a strong sense of community and place a high value on loyalty and solidarity with their own kind. They have a tendency to put the needs of the community above the needs of the individual. Many of them consider it essential to learn at least one foreign language, to play at least one instrument, and to know at least one trade, since most of their livelihood depends on trading with different races.

Hazrun
One of the continent’s native races and the third most numerous. The Hazrun were dominated for centuries by the Shun Dynasty. With the collapse of the old empire and its subsequent takeover by Ozumi, the Hazrun were finally free and massacred the remaining Rénshi in their traditional territory, later joining the few free Hazrun that remained, creating hybrid cultures with aspects of the culture of their former masters. To prevent another invasion and the enslavement of their people, the Hazrun militarised and today have large armies with highly efficient units, the result of their domestication of draconic species, such as drakes, wyverns, sauroids and avioserpes. Many returned to their old lifestyle as reindeer herders, hunters and fishermen to forget their detestable past under the rule of another race.
Their nation, known as the Jirkaeriya Confederacy, is ruled by a Soho (Hazrunic: leader, ruler, king), who must have “divine ancestry”. If the next leader is not elected peacefully, suitors can unify the cultures/tribes. The current Hazrun nation is the result of the conquest of Tazkiairga and his wife Huzur, who fought against Tazkiairga’s brothers to unify the hazrun race.
Hazrun culture is diverse, with several “peoples” within the same nation. The largest are Berihazrun (“Hazrun of the Plain”), Keiozhazrun (“Hazrun of the River”) and Damohazrun (“Hazrun of the Mountain”). Generally, women have short hair, letting it grow only after marriage, while the opposite occurs with men, who may also cut their hair during military service as a symbol of their “marriage to the nation”. Like the ancient elves, they do not have any body or facial hair. Women use midriff-revealing clothes while single to indicate they are available, but cover them up once they have boyfriends or husbands. The Hazrun wear earrings, necklaces and body paint with various symbols that other races do not understand. Wars and battles are mostly carried out by men only, as Hazrun women are naturally physically smaller and weaker. Despite this, it is said that a Hazrun woman is as strong as a man of another race.
The most peculiar characteristic of the hazrun is certainly the presence of horns, which are highly prized in all their cultures. They also have four fingers on each hand and foot, stronger nails and sharper fangs. Individuals with branched deer-like horns, called Adarkahazrun (“Branched Horned Person”), make up the “high caste” of hazrun, that is, clan heads, rulers and military leaders. The Hazrun view the hornless races as unworthy or dishonorable. They are not able to reproduce with other races, so it is more accurate to refer to them as another species. It is noted that they are very resistant to alcohol and cannot perceive spicy tastes very well.
As soon as they arrived on the new continent, the races coming from Pectus suspected a connection between the ancient Golofn, the Orcs and the Hazrun due to the presence of horns. Their origins are not known for sure and their origin myths do not tell of an exodus from distant lands. Furthermore, the Golofn were immortal, possessed extreme control of magic and had divine blood running through their veins, while the Hazrun appear to be ordinary mortals. Ancient accounts of the Sulkai and Shun do not clarify anything, since, wherever they came from, they were always in their lands before the other races.

Usagizok
They have a strong sense of balance and agility, allowing them to move quickly and gracefully through the natural landscapes. Usagizok developed unique cultural practices based on their connection to nature. They have a ritual for thanking the plants and animals they rely on for sustainability and have developed a system of using natural resources sustainably. Their enhanced hearing also plays a role in their culture. They have developed a form of communication at a frequency that only members of their own species can hear.
The Usagizok were enslaved by the Shun Dynasty for being exotic and were even seen as pets by some. This led to tensions between the two races even after the fall of the dynasty. The Usagizok have long ears like rabbits or hares, a fur-covered body, resistant claws for digging and very strong leg muscles that enable them to jump higher and further away than the other races. Their incisors are bigger and stronger due to their mostly vegetarian diet which consists mostly of root vegetables, leaves, and fruits. Some of them have short tails very similar to a rabbit’s. In terms of their current situation, the Usagizok are struggling to find their place in the world since being freed from slavery. They have difficulty integrating into other societies and prefer isolating themselves and live a more nomadic lifestyle in their partially underground warrens.
As a result of their enslavement, Usagizok are usually not taken seriously by other races. They may have difficulty finding work or housing outside of their own communities, and may face discrimination or violence. Despite this, the Usagizok have managed to carve out their own niche in society. They are skilled at jobs that require agility, such as acrobatics or hunting, and have developed a reputation as skilled scouts, mercenaries, assassins, and spies due to their heightened senses and physical abilities. Many Usagizok have withdrawn from the larger world and created their own isolated communities, hidden away in forests or other remote areas. These communities are wary of outsiders and have their own unique customs and traditions.
The Usagizok are matriarchal; a warren is mostly composed of related members descended from the same maternal ancestor. They are very fertile. A pregnancy lasts for only 4 months and the offspring, often born as quadruplets or triplets, reach childhood in 2 years and sexual maturity in 10. The females in the warren take turns nursing the newborns while the males cultivate plants or go out to trade, forage or hunt. To avoid inbreeding, they have a tradition of visiting other warrens to find suitable spouses. A matriarch can have multiple husbands. Like the Hazrun, they cannot interbreed with other races
Usagizok are grappling with their own internal divisions and conflicts between different tribes and factions. This is related both to differences in religious or cultural practices and by more pragmatic concerns such as access to resources or disputes over leadership.

Outsider
The Outsiders’ arrival into Yuandi remains an event cloaked in mystery and subject to much philosophical debate among the continent’s scholars and sages. While some theorise a conflict against the Theoclasts, others whisper of a vengeful deity tearing the very fabric of the cosmos, banishing these beings to a plane not their own. Such a cataclysmic event likely didn’t occur without leaving scars, both on the lands of Yuandi and the essence of the Outsiders themselves.
Over the 72 years since their appearance, the Outsiders have become a norm within the continent’s landscapes, yet they do not form associations or clans of their own; instead, they are unified by their shared displacement and the longing to understand their origin and purpose.
The physical form of Outsiders is both alien and mesmerising. Their height can vary drastically, with smooth skin that radiates soft light at dusk. Their unique tentacle-like hair structures suggest an evolved form not limited to the aesthetic, with some Outsiders found to communicate or manipulate objects with these appendages. The absence of aging signs makes their lifespan a subject of much curiosity, as no Outsider has shown any decline or deterioration over their time in Yuandi.
With no memories of their own culture or names, Outsiders have come to adopt appellations and customs from the societies they integrate themselves into, often taking on roles as scholars, artisans, diplomats, or advisors. Their unique perspectives unclouded by personal pasts or ambitions make them intriguing and sometimes unsettling company.
Though their integration varies by region and society, many Outsiders have earned a place of respect, for their impartial outlook and ability to see beyond the distraction of mortal prejudices. In some cultures, they’ve been considered omens of significant change or figures of worship, existing as bridges between the outer realms and the Eartly Realm.
Outsiders perplex the inhabitants of Yuandi not only with their origin but with their method of reproduction — or lack thereof. No new Outsider has been observed to come into being since their first appearance on the continent. This unusual trait has led to numerous theories: that the Outsiders are limited, a finite number of beings with no way to perpetuate their kind, or perhaps they simply have not encountered the conditions needed to initiate their reproductive cycles on Yuandi. Strangely, they exhibit sexual dimorphism, apparently having distinctions between males and females.
The Outsiders are known for their most notable and enigmatic ability: transient phasing. This rare power allows them to become intangible at unpredictable moments, causing them to slip through solid objects, evade physical attacks, or even sink into the earth, only to re-emerge unharmed. Such occurrences are sporadic and uncontrollable, often correlated with their emotional state or environmental stimuli, hinting at a possible connection to an underlying psychic or dimensional trait inherent to their being.
While this ability is viewed with awe and a palpable sense of wonder by other inhabitants of Yuandi, it is also a source of fear and suspicion. Those who encounter Outsiders experiencing moments of phasing can’t help but question the nature of these ethereal wanderers and their place in the world.
Outsiders tend to avoid positions of overt power or leadership unless it serves a purpose that benefits greater societal good. They are pacifists by necessity, as direct conflict could trigger abilities they cannot control, yet their very presence can impact the results of warring factions. It’s not uncommon for Outsiders to serve as mediators and negotiators, given their unaffiliated and unbiased nature.

Half-demon
Demons have always been present across all cultures in Yuandi as antagonistic forces or tricksters. Now left without a master after ALMF’s disappearance, anarchy reigns in Hell. Many demons fled across the dimensions, though only on the Earthly Realm inside Ma’at’s barrier did they find respite. Many disguised themselves as mythological creatures, minor deities, and nature spirits familiar to the cultures of Yuandi to the point that the “new mythology” made mortals distrust the supernatural. There are specialised orders of exorcists who hunt demons, as well as angels, who are their natural enemies due to their masters’ eternal quarrel.
Half-demons have a demon as one of the parents and can exhibit demonic physical traits, such as differently coloured skin, red or golden eyes, fangs, higher or lower body temperature, among other miscellaneous traits. The one that appears most consistently is an affinity towards magic, more frequently dark magic or whatever element the demon parent was associated with. Half-demons are not necessarily evil and are capable of good as much as the other fully mortal races.
Due to their demonic heritage, half-demons attract supernatural entities with the most varied purposes. Wandering spirits who still have grudges or unfinished affairs from the time when they were living seek out half-demons, urging them to help them find peace. However, not all half-demons are attuned to such entities and their words manifest as simple intrusive thoughts or strange dreams. Half-demons are also more resistant to possession, mind-reading, and hypnosis.

Angel
After YHVH’s death/capture at the hands of the Theoclasts, angels regained their free will but were left without purpose. Many still work for the Church of YHVH, spreading hope to the faithful about the future lives they can have in Paradise if they follow YHVH’s teachings.
However, tainted by the sin from the Earthly Realm, some angels learnt the evils of the world and lost part of their light. Those angels have black wings and are called “Fallen Ones” by the other angels. Still, angels with black wings aren’t necessarily unaligned with YHVH. Special task forces who execute justice across the continent have black wings from eliminating threats and sinners, thus being exposed to the stench of death. They function not too much unlike mercenaries.
Angels with grey or white wings retained more of their light and are often associated with non-violent activities, such as priesthood, healing, and preaching. All angels with no exception have lost their almighty power that was provided by YHVH, who also suppressed their free will, thus being considerably weaker than their versions from 500 years ago. Still, mortals respect them as symbols of YHVH’s divine power and benevolence. Even people who don’t worship YHVH approve of the angels’ activities, since they help the communities around them.
When an angel’s physical form is dissipated (that is, when they’re killed), they revert to an Angel Core, a crystal-like artefact imbued with divine essence. As the years pass, the body is reformed, though the memories are lost. The process is more often used to “rescue” fallen angels so that they can be reborn free of sin.

abstract

We address the problem of the electromagnetic radiation produced by charge distributions in the framework of a semiclassical approach proposed in the work by Bagrov, Gitman, Shishmarev and Farias [J. Synchrotron Rad. (2020). 27, 902-911]. In this approach, currents, generating the radiation are considered classically, while the quantum nature of the radiation is kept exactly.
Quantum states of the electromagnetic field are solutions of Schrödinger's equation and relevant quantities to the problem are evaluated with the aid of transition probabilities. This construction allows us to introduce the quantum transition time in physical quantities and assess its role in radiation problems by classical currents.
We study radiated electromagnetic energies in detail and present a definition for the rate at which radiation is emitted from sources. In calculating the total energy and rate radiated by a pointlike charged particle accelerated by a constant and uniform electric field, we discover

Introduction

It is known that a change in the state of motion of charged particles is usually accompanied by an electromagnetic radiation. The most prominent examples are the radiation of accelerated charges undergoing rectilinear motion and of charges performing circular motion. The most adequate and accurate description of the process should be carried out in the framework of QED; see e.g.
Refs. . However, in a number of cases, specific technical difficulties arising from the direct application of the QED formalism can be avoided resorting to approximations, which often allows one quite accurately unveiling the essence of the physical effect. Here, the so-called classical description of the effect is most often used, which is as follows: the motion of charged particles is considered within the framework of classical (nonrelativistic or relativistic) mechanics, then using Maxwell's equations, the electromagnetic field generated by this motion is restored (for example, in the form of Liénard-Wiechert potentials), finally, the assumption is made (which corresponds to an approximation) that the observed electromagnetic radiation generated by the motion of the charges must be calculated as the energy flux determined by the Umov-Poynting vector, see e.g.
Refs. . For example, in the framework of the classical description, a formula for the angular distribution of the synchrotron radiation power was obtained by Schott . An alternative derivation of this result and its deep analysis, especially for high-energy relativistic electrons, was given by Schwinger .
The essence of quantum corrections to the classical result was first pointed out in Ref. . QED calculation of such corrections was presented in Ref. within the Furry picture (based on exact solutions of the Dirac equations with a magnetic field). In the framework of the source theory , Schwinger had presented an original derivation of similar results .
The electromagnetic radiation produced by a uniformly accelerated charged particle was from the beginning a subject of theoretical debate. The central aspect of the discussion was the question of whether such a particle could radiate at all or not. One of the arguments contrary to the radiation was raised by Pauli , who calculated the electromagnetic fields produced by the particle and concluded that such a particle could not radiate since the corresponding fields did not contain wave-like contributions.
In order to reach this conclusion, Pauli used results obtained earlier by Born and elements of conformal invariance of Maxwell's equations. On the other hand, years earlier, Schott had calculated the electromagnetic fields radiated by the accelerated particle and computed the energy rate through the Poynting's theorem.
He discovered that the energy emission rate is proportional to the square of the particle's acceleration and mentioned that his result was in agreement with the Larmor's classical result , currently known as the Larmor's formula . The most compelling arguments in favor of the radiation were later given by Fulton and Rohrlich in Refs.
. In these works, the authors presented a thorough discussion of the relevant publications and calculated the energy and momentum emission rate in a covariant form. Few years later, Nikishov and Ritus, using Landau-Lifshitz formula for the spectral distribution of the emitted electromagnetic energy , had calculated the energy spectrum and the energy emission rate in a covariant form .
More recently, Eriksen and Gron extensively discussed the problem in a series of papers and presented a study of radiation reaction effects. At present, it is widely accepted that uniformly accelerated particles radiate, and the classical derivation of its energy rate is presented in many textbooks; see e.g.
Refs. . In the work , it was proposed the so-called semiclassical approach for describing quantum properties of radiation of currents of charged particles. In this approach, currents, generating the radiation are considered classically, whereas the quantum nature of the radiation is taken into account exactly.
Universal formulas describing multiphoton radiation were derived. The approach does not require knowledge of the exact solutions of relativistic wave equations with external fields; hence technical difficulties associated with the use of the Furry picture do not arise. Moreover, the semiclassical approach can be applied to any trajectory performed by the particle, even including cases with backreaction, as these can be accounted for by solving the Lorentz equations with radiation-reaction terms.
We note that in the framework of the semiclassical approach one can directly calculate the radiation emitted from any trajectory of a charged particle, whereas, in QED, the technics of calculating photon transition amplitudes (let say in the Furry picture) is adopted only for charge motions caused by external electromagnetic fields.
However, an univocal correspondence between every charge trajectory and a corresponding electromagnetic field does not exist. The efficacy of the semiclassical approach was demonstrated in calculating synchrotron and undulator radiations. In the present article we apply the semiclassical approach to study electromagnetic radiation by uniformly accelerated charged particles.
In Sect. 2 we present the basic formulation of the semiclassical description of electromagnetic radiation in the general case, refining and supplementing the results presented in the original Refs. . In Sect. 3, we apply these results to calculate electromagnetic energies and rates radiated by an accelerated charge.
In Sect. 4, we compare the obtained results with the above cited calculations by other authors.

Discussion

In this work, we address the problem of the electromagnetic radiation produced by charge distributions in a semiclassical approach, in which the radiation field is quantum while current densities-sources of radiation-are regarded classically. In this formulation, quantum states of the electromagnetic field are exact solutions of Schrödinger's equation, whose Hamiltonian describes both free photons as well as their interaction with external currents.
On this basis, pertinent electromagnetic quantities such as energies and energy rates radiated by currents, are calculated with the aid of transition probabilities between states with well-defined number of photons. This construction enables us to introduce, rigorously, the quantum transition time as a "radiation interval" and to assess its role in radiation problems.
More specifically, assuming the vacuum as the initial state, we calculated time-dependent one-photon, multiphoton, total electromagnetic energies, and the rate at which the radiation is emitted from the source; the latter, in particular, presented for the first time. It must be noted that time is intrinsically absent in classical electrodynamics, as the electromagnetic energy and rate are usually derived through Poynting's and Parseval's theorem.
We discovered that our formulas for the total energy and rate are compatible with the corresponding classical results in the limit where the quantum transition interval tends to infinity. Moreover, all quantities obtained in the semiclassical approach are valid to any current distribution as well as the nature of the external force field responsible for their acceleration.
To illustrate the use of the semiclassical approach, we study a simple yet intriguing physical system: the pointlike charged particle accelerated by a constant and uniform electric field. We present a detailed consideration of the total energy and rate radiated by the particle, both in cases where it performs a general trajectory in the space as when it moves parallel to the field.
Our expression for the total energy is time-dependent and coincides with the classical result in the large-time limit. We derive an asymptotic approximation for the angular-spectral distribution of the total energy and represent it graphically, considering the external field fixed but varying the radiation interval.
Our results show a typical radiation pattern of linearly accelerated charged particles: the pattern has lobes tipped toward the direction of motion. Similar patterns are also seen in the pictures for the energy emission rate. Besides electromagnetic energies, we derived time-dependent expressions for the total energy rate radiated by the particle.
After integrating it over the angles and momentum, we discovered that our result differs from Larmor's by a factor of 1/3. This discrepancy is due to a difference in the definition of energy rate. In classical electrodynamics, the rate is defined through Parseval's theorem, while in the semiclassical formulation, the rate is defined as the time derivative of the energy.
As discussed above, the absence of this factor was pointed out before by Nikishov and Ritus in in the context of the classical theory by effectively differentiating the total energy with respect to time. We conclude this work by emphasizing that the semiclassical approach offers an alternative description of physical systems interacting with background fields.
Despite being an approximation compared to QED, the semiclassical formulation exactly incorporates the quantum character of the electromagnetic field. For this reason, this theory allows extracting information about electromagnetic properties stemming from the interaction between radiation and matter beyond the reach of classical electrodynamics.
We hope that the ideas discussed in this work might help study more complex systems, e.g., involving complicated external fields whose analytical forms do not admit to solving relativistic wave equations exactly, thus precluding the use of Furry representation.

Christoph Carsten: Animal Play and the Affect of Language 
I 
Since the mid-1990s there has been an increasing interest in theories of affect, not only in 
philosophy or media and cultural studies but also in the arts, neuroscience or cognitive science. 
What these different approaches have in common is an uneasiness about the strong focus on 
language in theories such as poststructuralism, which have been dominating the field of the 
humanities for decades. What is criticized are not the achievements of poststructuralism in 
general but mainly its one-sided focus on language, which subsumes every possible dimension 
of experience under the total reign of the significant.1 Karen Barad puts it concisely in her 
dictum: “Language has been granted too much power.”2 
The turning away from language-centered theories had several consequences within the 
humanities: On the one hand, a lot of recent affect theories prefer art forms as their objects of 
investigation which are not predominantly linguistic, such as film, dance, performances but also 
architecture or media art. At this point we can already see that in many cases the turning away 
from language went hand in hand with a decoupling of language and affect which resulted in a 
new dichotomy of language on the one side and affect on the other. Furthermore, a lot of 
theories of affect link their critique of the dominance of language to a critique of the dominance 
of the human, that is an implicit anthropocentrism, which for them can be found in most of the 
language centered theories, including poststructuralism. Despite its declared antihumanism, in 
poststructuralism the decentered human subject was simply replaced by the notions of language 
and culture, respectively. However, language and culture are themselves two of the main 
concepts which historically have been invoked to establish the notion of the exceptional 
position of the human. In so far, a poststructuralist world is a human world – even if the subjects 
are decentered and not masters in their own houses anymore. Animals, plants, matter, things or 
ghosts – they all are only thinkable as linguistic enunciations, that is social constructions, in 
this perspective, without being granted any kind of self-activity or agency. This critique of 
anthropocentrism has recently culminated in the declaration of a nonhuman turn. 3 
These results, which could only be outlined here in a rough and quite polemical way, seem to 
be quite comprehensible at first sight. However, they become astonishing when one looks at 
                                                           
1 Cf. Guattari, Félix: Chaosmosis. An Ethico-Aesthetic Paradigm. Translated by Paul Bains and Julian Pefanis. 
Bloomington, Indianapolis: Indiana University Press, 1995. p. 5.  
2 Barad, Karen: Posthumanist Performativity. Toward an Understanding of How Matter Comes to Matter. In: 
Signs. Journal of Women in Culture and Society. Vol. 28, no. 3. p. 801-831. p. 801.  
3 Cf.: The Nonhuman Turn. Ed. by Richard Grusin. Minneapolis, London: University of Minnesota Press, 2015. 
the work of Brian Massumi himself, who stands as a precursor for a lot of these tendencies and 
developments within the humanities. Indeed, Massumi differentiates language and affect in his 
famous essay The Autonomy of Affect, which was first published in 1995.4 According to him, 
affects are prepersonal, not yet qualified intensities, which manifest themselves in relational 
events, and which, at the same time, transform the capabilities of the body to affect and to be 
affected. Affects do not follow the logic of semantic qualification and express themselves as 
autonomic bodily reactions, which do not necessarily have to be registered subjectively. The 
notion of affect describes a moment of suspense, of a potential disruption, full of movement, 
intensity and resonance, which cannot be directed towards particular, preformed aims or ends. 
This is the point where affects can be distinguished from emotions or categorical affects, which, 
according to Massumi are the discursive classification of the felt quality of an experience, 
which, retrospectively, pins down the intensity of an experience to conventional patterns and 
categories, and, in the process, transforms the affective event to a personal, subjective 
experience. This distinction shows that affect withdraws especially from the qualifying and 
signifying functions of language, which is here understood as a conventional system of 
differences. Affects rather operate on the level of intensities and effects, whereas language 
operates on the level of content and form as well as “narrativizable action-reaction-circuits, (…) 
function and meaning”5. However, and this is important, according to Massumi, language and 
affect can never be fully separated, although they are functioning according to different logics: 
They are two different tendencies, but which are two sides of the same processual coin in every 
expression-event. Massumi writes: „Language, though headstrong, is not simply in opposition 
to intensity. It would seem to function differentially in relation to it. […] The relationship 
between the levels of intensity and qualification is not one of conformity or correspondence but 
rather of resonation or interference, amplification or dampening.”6 For Massumi, language and 
affect are “two dimensions of every expression, one superlinear, the other linear.”7 Against this 
background, Massumi cannot be read as a proponent of a disqualification of language or the 
imperative to assume a primacy of the affective. Instead, we will have to look at the singular 
ways in which linguistic and affective dimensions are always already entangled in expression-
events, the ways in which they resonate, interfere, amplify or dampen each other. 
                                                           
4 Cf. Massumi, Brian: Parables for the Virtual. Movement, Affect, Sensation. Durham & London: Duke University 
Press, 2002. P. 23-45. 
5 Ibid. p. 26. 
6 Ibid. p. 25. 
7 Ibid. p. 27.  
In the following, this shall be done by reference to two examples: On the one hand on the basis 
of animal play as it is analyzed by Massumi, following Gregory Bateson, and on the other hand 
via the concept of becoming-animal in literature, which has been established by Gilles Deleuze 
and Félix Guattari in their book on Kafka and in A Thousand Plateaus. In the course of this, the 
leading question of my analysis is twofold: In the first instance I would like to consider the 
ways in which language and affect are entangled in the particular examples. After that I would 
like to reflect for a moment on the question which consequences this might have for our thinking 
about the distinction between animals and humans, which, historically, has for a long time been 
constructed by distinguishing those who can from those who cannot speak. 
II 
In 1992 Gregory Bateson visits the Fleishhacker Zoo in San Francisco in order to learn 
something about the evolutionary principles of communication. He is especially interested in 
the question if the ability to recognize signals as signals, which Bateson views as the basic 
requirement for the emergence of communication, can already be found in animals. During his 
visit Bateson becomes witness of the play fight of two apes. According to Bateson, it was 
obvious, even for the not involved spectator, that the gestures of the apes were similar to the 
gestures of a real fight, but that there was nevertheless a difference. Furthermore, it was also 
obvious that the apes knew as well that they were not really fighting but playing.8 For Bateson, 
the playful gestures of the apes could be summarized in the following statement: “These actions 
in which we now engage [play] do not denote what those actions for which they stand [fight] 
would denote.” 9 A nipping in play denotes a bite, but at the same time it says that it does not 
denote what a real bite would denote since “this is play”. However, to be able to recognize that 
a certain gesture belongs to the mode of existence of play and not of fight means to be able to 
identify signals as signals. Therefore, in animal play we already find metacommunicative 
capabilities. For Bateson, this metacommunicative dimension of language evolutionarily comes 
before the production of denotative messages. This could not be different because, as Bateson 
says: “Denotative communication as it occurs at the human level is only possible after the 
evolution of a complex set of metalinguistic (but not verbalized) rules which govern how words 
and sentences shall be related to objects and events. It is therefore appropriate to look for the 
evolution of such metalinguistic and/or meta-communicative rules at a prehuman and preverbal 
                                                           
8 cf. Bateson, Gregory: Steps to an Ecology of Mind. Collected Essays in Anthropology, Psychiatry, Evolution 
and Epistemology. Northvale, New Jersey: Jason Aronson Inc., 1987. p. 139. 
9 Ibid. Emphasis in the original.  
level.”10 Evolutionary, animal play can be viewed as a significant step within the development 
of language, human language included. Or, as Massumi puts it: “Animal play creates the 
conditions for language.” 11 
In his reading of Bateson’s text Brian Massumi is especially interested in the question of how 
animals know that the movements of the opponent are playful gestures and not actions in a real 
combat. Why is there no insertion of an escape or defending reflex? Massumi comes to the 
conclusion that this is because of a minimal stylistic difference between the playful gesture and 
the analog gesture in a real fight. The metacommunicative statement “this is Play” is not 
expressed by means of linguistic signs or cognition but is directly embodied in the style of the 
performance of the playful gesture. The how” of the performance, its “-esqueness”12, as 
Massumi calls it, produces a qualitative surplus, which indicates the difference between play 
and combat. The playful gesture can never be fully captured in terms of functionality, there is 
always a qualitative excess. That is why it could be called aesthetic.  
Massumi now links this aesthetic dimension of animal metacommunication to Daniel Stern’s 
concept of vitality affects. Vitality affects are “qualities of feeling [which] do not fit into our 
existing lexicon or taxonomy of affects.”13 They are about changes in intensity over time, which 
are better captured in “dynamic, kinetic terms, such as ‘surging,’ ‘fading away,’ ‘fleeting,’ 
‘explosive,’ ‘crescendo,’ ‘decrescendo,’ ‘bursting,’ ‘drawn out,’ and so on.”14 Whereas 
categorical affects deal with the “what” of a concrete emotion, for example joy, anger, grief, 
and so on, vitality affects concern the felt “how” of an experience, the style of a performance 
and its immediately felt qualities. Daniel Stern gives an example to illustrate the expressivity 
of vitality affects: a puppet show. The puppet has restricted or no capacities to show categorical 
affects, for example via facial expressions. However, when it comes to vitality affects its margin 
of maneuver is much bigger, since the puppet is capable of a wide range of potential 
movements. Other examples would be abstract dance or music.15 
In the performative gestures of the playing apes, the meta-comment “this is play” is embodied 
in the minimal stylistic difference between the playful gesture and the real fighting gesture, 
which is immediately felt as a vitality affect by the animals involved. In this situation,
