“Wow, you own two champions !” Exclaimed Lance. The lion chuckled before calling out a third cheetah, another male jubatus. “I might have a third one if he was not so unruly.” That cheetah cast a strange look at Ash before being seized by the enormous lion fingers. “Come here you !” Rumbled the lion before putting him with the two other cheetahs.
“I never saw you here before.” Said the lion while examining his three cheetahs. He carefully seized their legs between his huge fingers and stretched them out delicately as to check their state. “And you come with a pardinensis and he finishes among the first ten.” Said Bassari with a smile.
“It was not the most difficult race.” Replied Lance, "I wanted something easy for him for the first time. " Ash started when he heard Lance said “for the first time” doe he intended to make him run again ?
“Indeed replied the lion. I usually use this one as a warm-up for mines.”
“Yes, I heard it was the reason most cheetah doesn’t have their best performances at this one, they save themselves for the next and more serious races. Your’s must be great when they put all their strengths into !”
Ash was proud to have been in the top ten, but he put all hi strength in this race, and hearing most of the other competitors were in fact saving themselves made him feel downcast.
“I hope they will be.” Said the lion with a smirk. “But your cheetah makes quite an impression. I didn’t see a pardinensis on this track for years, if ever you wish to sell him, feel free to contact me, I’m ready to put the price to have him, or if you want a skilled champion I would be happy to trade one of mines with your pardinensis.” Bassari looked down at Ash with a smile. Ash started to move backward but he saw Lance lifted the heel of one of his huge feet and tapped it on the ground.
Lance was also surprised by the words of the lion. “No, sorry, I don’t want to sell him.” Replied the jaguar. “And I’m still trying to tame and train him, it’s a wild micro, he doesn’t always behave properly you know.” The lion chuckled. He seized the third cheetah by the scruff and lifted him to show him to Lance. “I’m used to unruly micros.” He teasingly shifted the cheetah and released him in his huge cupped hand. “You just have to be patient, although I concur an adult and perhaps middle aged wild one might impose some challenges.”
Both giants saw the preparations for the next race were almost finished.
“Will you make him take part to the next races ?” Asked Bassari.
“I don’t think I will, replied Lance. It must have been a lot for him already. I see he is struggling to behave with all the other macros at proximity and this bustle, he is not used to it.”
“I see, replied the giant lion. I think he should have enough energy for another race, although he might not reach the same ranking this time. But lot of cheetahs owners present here would like to see him run.”
Lance smiled and looked down at Ash. The grey furred cheetah was not liking to have to remain close of the lion, and he was glad Lance allowed him to stay on the ground instead to be held in his hand at a closer place from Bassari.
“So then, Ash. What do you think of it ? Do you want to try another race or stop right now ?”

Ash didn’t reached the top ten this time. But Lance was proud of him nevertheless. The grey furred cheetah was exhausted and almost collapsed on the floor of the track. Lance was about to come to pick him up but he was stopped by a massive bull who told him no macros were allowed to walk on the race track for safety measure toward the micros.
Lance scooped Ash in his massive hands when the pardinensis reached the rim of the track and the jaguar moved to a table of the bar of the venue.
“You performed very well ! Consider your punishment lifted !” Said Lance.
“Thank you Master.” Replied Ash. “What rank did I reach ?”
“You’re 18th, out of 32 contestants. But you did it, you overcame your fears and followed the rules. When I explained to Bassari you was a wild one captured from only some weeks he was impressed you didn’t try to run away.”
About the macro lion, his cheetahs performed well, Ran was third, Lene the female was fifth and Laar the unruly one was eighth. Lance saw Bassari was getting them back in his hands.
He smiled and poured some water from on bottle in its cap and offered it to Ash who was still panting from the late race. As the bottle was scaled for macros Ash could barely lift the cap full of water and Lance had to help him.
“Oh, you should use it instead.” Said Bassari as he moved at the table of Lance. He showed a strip where were attached several diminutive bottles scaled to the size of a micro. “It’s easier for them.” The gigantic anthropomorphic lion carefully used the tip of the huge claws of his thumb and forefinger to detach one of the bottles. He gave it to Lance, knowing Ash would be nervous too much to accept to have the huge hand of an unknown macro coming close of him. Lance thanked the lion and looked at it, his eyes squinting to read some diminutive letters, he saw it was only written “north mounts water”.
“Here Ash. For you.” Ash took it and thanked both Lance and the lion. He smelled at the opening of the bottle after having open it but as he saw the three cheetahs of the lion were drinking the same kind of bottle he sipped at it. The water was fresh, more than the one of the bottle of Lance ordered from the bar of the place and it was way easier to drink in this bottle scaled at his size.
Ash saw the lion ordered a red colored drink, but he doubted it was alcohol.
There was two races reserved to micro canidae were African wild dogs, chacals and coyotes were running. This race was timed the way to allow the cheetahs to relax some before a third race. Ash watched some moments of it from the vast screens placed on the walls, he found it enthralling and somewhat understood the interest these macros had for it.
A male macro hyena approached. “Congratulation Mister Arouk ! Your micros were spectacular tonight !” He looked at Lance. “And thank you for the show, your cheetah got attention, several spectators and enthusiasts posted photos of him on the net.” Ash stopped to drink when the hyena started to speak at his master. As a former wild micro used to live hidden and unnoticed, he was not enjoying the idea to draw attention from the macros at all.
“I knew pardinensis were rare, but I was not aware he would draw so much attention in a place like this.” Replied Lance.
“It’s the first time I see one alive.” Replied the hyena. Ash’s ears pricked up as he heard the word “alive”. “There are not so much enthusiasts who own one.” Continued the hyena. “Perhaps you should get in touch with some other owners, the ones who have a female might be interested to get cubs.” Ash was not liking this idea at all, and seeing Lance looking interested made the pardinensis cheetah feeling worried.
“I know one of them.” Said Bassari. “But even when you have a couple, it’s not easy to make them reproduce. At least naturally.”

Can you write a hypothetical alternate plot for the manga Gate JSDF, only in this version the US military, the Philippine military and the South Korean military arr invited to join into the other world with the JSDF, and the US military is represented by the Rat Patrol ftom Metal Gear Solid 4 lead by Meryl Silverburgh accompanied by Old Snake and Otacon, the Philippine military comprises the cast of 2003's Philippine comedy Asboobs Asal Bobo which comprises of an ice cream vendor was bullied and thrown on a river and he swore to become a brave soldier, joining him include a spoiled brat snaps his adopted uncle and forced him to undergo military training, a barangay tanod or a neighborhood watchman in thecPhilippine language who is an action freak who mauled even the well wishers for his birthday, a NEET who accidentally burned a whole building while he was in an internet cafe and was offered to be a soldier by his roommate and a mama's boy who joins the military to strengthen his manhood and erase his mama's boy image, and the South Korean military comprises adult versions of the cast of the manhwa Girls of the Wild’s including the manhwa’s characters Jaeoh Hwang, Yeojoeung Kim, and Gangrok Choi since conscription in South Korea is mandatory, making it some crossover, how would their interactions be with Itami Tomita, Kuribayashi and the rest of the JSDF? And their interactions with the empire especially with Princess Pina and Prince Zorzal, Rory, Yao, Lelei and Tuka, and the scenarios? How do they play out in these episodes: 1"The Self-Defence Force Goes to Another World"
A mysterious gate suddenly appears in Ginza, Tokyo, through which mythological creatures led by men in Roman armor emerge and attack the people. Yōji Itami, a JSDF reservist who is attending a nearby doujin convention, helps organizing the police to evacuate the civilians to the Imperial Palace before the JSDF arrives to stop the invaders. For his actions, Itami is promoted to First Lieutenant and celebrated as a national hero. The appearance of the Gate and attack on Japanese civilians, dubbed the Ginza Incident, prompts the incumbent Prime Minister to take action by proclaiming that Japan will send a JSDF task force backed by the US to the "Special Region", the world beyond the Gate, to not only explore the new world but also capture and demand reparations from those responsible for the attack. After three months of preparation, the new Prime Minister sends off the JSDF task force, including Itami, on their mission to the Special Region. Upon arriving, the task force encounters an army waiting for them, and prepares for battle.
2"Two Military Forces"
The army sent by the Empire to deal with the Japanese forces stationed at Alnus Hill, where the Gate is located, is easily obliterated by the JSDF's modern artillery. Emperor Molt calls for the armies of the Empire's vassal states to attack, only for them to be defeated with massive casualties as well; a move planned by the Emperor to prevent the vassal states from taking advantage of the Empire's depleted military. While Emperor Molt decides to delay a possible advance from the JSDF, Itami is assigned to lead the 3rd Recon Unit, created to survey the nearby cities and points of interest. After passing by the village of Coda, the 3rd Unit observes a massive Fire Dragon burning and destroying a settlement within the nearby forest. While looking for survivors, Itami finds an unconscious Elf woman inside a well.
3"Fire Dragon"
Taking the Elf with them, the 3rd Unit return to the village of Coda, and upon learning of the Fire Dragon, the villagers decide to evacuate, assisted by the Japanese soldiers. The group, now including all the villagers, are later joined by two mages, Lelei la Lalena and her master Kato El Altestan. Hoping to take advantage of the situation, a group of bandits decide to attack the villagers, only to be slaughtered by Rory Mercury, an apostle of the Dark God Emroy. While escorting the refugees, Itami's party encounter Rory, who decides to accompany them as well. However, the Fire Dragon appears and attacks the convoy, killing numerous villagers until the 3rd Unit blows off one of its front legs with an anti-tank rocket, forcing it to retreat. After the 3rd Unit parts ways with the villagers, Itami decides to take the remaining refugees, as well as Rory, the Elf woman, and Lelei, back to Alnus Hill. 

4"To Unknown Lands"
The 3rd Recon Unit returns to Alnus Hill, now converted into an advanced JSDF base, and Itami obtains authorization to provide shelter to the refugees. Meanwhile, Princess Piña Co Lada from the Empire learns more about the JSDF's exploits and decides to investigate them personally. Back at Alnus, the refugees get used to their new lives among the Japanese soldiers, but for some reason Tuka Luna Marceau, the Elf girl, keeps requesting supplies not only for herself, but for another, unknown male not listed among the guests. Knowing that they cannot depend on the JSDF's charity forever, Lelei points out that they can collect scales from the corpses of dragons killed by JSDF, which will fetch a good price in the local markets. Meanwhile, on the other side of the gate, the Japanese Diet requests Itami for an audience regarding the battle against the Fire Dragon. However, by the time the summons for Itami arrives, he has already left with Rory, Lelei, Tuka and the rest of the 3rd Unit to trade the collected dragon scales at the city of Italica, where Piña and her Knights are also headed in search of further information about the JSDF.
5"The Battle of Italica"
Itami's party arrives at Italica, just as the city's forces, led by Princess Piña, repel an assault by an invading bandit force made up of deserters from the armies defeated at Alnus. Knowing that her knights and the local militia lack the strength to keep holding off the bandits until help arrives, Piña finds herself in a predicament until she meets the 3rd Recon Unit. Upon being informed of the situation, Itami decides to help defend the city and agrees with Piña's plan of positioning himself and his soldiers on the least guarded side of the walls (the South Gate) to act as a decoy. However, the enemy does not fall for their trap and launches an attack on the main force at the East Gate instead. As the city's defenses are broken, the Princess finds herself on the verge of despair. 

6"Ride of the Valkyries"
Rory, Itami and two of his subordinates, Akira Tomita and Shino Kuribayashi, head to Piña's location to help her men. Meanwhile, the JSDF sends a helicopter unit to assist the 3rd Recon Unit in defending Italica, which arrives just in time, blasting Wagner's Ride of the Valkyries from loudspeakers and annihilating the invaders with ease. After Lelei sells the dragon scales and Itami has negotiated with Piña and the Italicans for rather trivial compensation terms in exchange for their retaining their sovereignty, the 3rd Recon Unit departs back to Alnus Hill, only to encounter Piña's Order of the Rose Knights on their way. Upon discovering their identities as JSDF members, the knights take Itami captive, unaware of the peace treaty he and Piña just established. In order to avoid further conflict, Itami orders his unit to leave without him instead of fighting, leaving himself at the knights' mercy. 

7"The Princess's Decision"
Back in Italica, Piña reprimands her knights Bozes and Panache for capturing Itami, fearing that the JSDF will use the incident as an excuse to retaliate for breaking the treaty. As the Formal family staff treat Itami's wounds, Rory, Lelei, Tuka and some of the 3rd Unit sneak back to Italica to rescue Itami, but find themselves welcomed by the Formal maids and join Itami for a small socializing party. Meanwhile, Piña orders Bozes to sleep with Itami in the hopes of earning his forgiveness, but Bozes becomes angry and assaults Itami after seeing him enjoying himself and seemingly ignoring her. Appalled that Bozes might have antagonized Itami further, Piña and Bozes join the 3rd Recon Unit's trip back to Alnus Hill to personally apologize to Itami's superiors for Bozes' actions. While Piña and Bozes meet with Itami's commanding officer Lieutenant General Hazama with Lelei as an interpreter, Itami invites Tuka to come with him to Japan to meet the Japanese Diet as a representative of the Special Region. The next day, Itami, Shino and Akira accompany Rory, Lelei, Tuka, Piña and Bozes through the Gate to Japan.
8"Japan, Beyond the Gate"
Itami and his group arrive in Tokyo, where Piña and the others girls are awed by the city and its people. After meeting a Public Security agent by the name of Komakado, Itami, Rory, Lelei, and Tuka head to the Japanese Diet while Piña and Bozes meet with members of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to discuss the details for the upcoming peace talks. At the Japanese Diet, Itami, Rory, Lelei, and Tuka are questioned by the chairwoman of the Investigation Committee on the Fire Dragon attack, who accuses the JSDF of failing to protect the refugees killed by the Fire Dragon. Rory, Lelei, and Tuka defend the JSDF, telling of how the Japanese soldiers helped save many lives from the monster. Afterwards, both Itami's and Piña's groups reunite in the subway to escape from the press as well as a mysterious group which seems to be targeting the Special Region girls. Due to a mole leaking their itinerary, Itami makes a change of plans and brings the group to stay with his ex-wife.
9"The Hakone Mountain Night Battle"
Itami explains everything to his ex-wife Risa, who agrees to help him by taking Rory, Lelei and Tuka on a shopping trip the next day, while Akira accompanies Piña and Bozes to the library after both of them take an interest in boys-love manga from Risa. Meanwhile, Itami meets with his old friend, Defense Minister Kanou Tarou, who instructs him to bring the Special Region guests to a hot spring inn guarded by the Japanese SFG. As Itami's group stays at the inn for some relaxation, three different Black Ops teams enter the area and battle with the SFG. While the SFG identifies two of the Black Ops operatives as Americans, the Japanese Prime Minister is blackmailed by the US President, who wants the SFG to stop attacking his Black Ops team so they can take the Special Region guests with them. The Prime Minister orders Tarou to tell his men to stand down, but not before revealing that he will be resigning to void the President's leverage. As the three Ops teams head to the Inn, Itami encounters a drunken and aroused Rory. 

10"Despair and Hope"
Rory's attempts to seduce Itami are interrupted by a phone call from Tarou. The US Black Ops team arrives at the Inn, only to encounter the two rival teams from Russia and China, leading to a three-way firefight which Rory soon joins, ending with everyone besides Rory dead. After taking a van from the Russians, Itami's group heads back to Ginza, but, worried that the foreign agents will attack again, Risa posts a message on the internet that the Special Region girls will be visiting the Ginza memorial. As a result, a large crowd gathers at Ginza to meet the girls, hindering the foreign agents' plans to kidnap them. Public Security is able to inconspicuously arrest all foreign agents on the scene, and after Shino publicizes the previous kidnapping attempts on live TV through her news reporter sister Nanami, the US, Chinese, and Russian leaders cancel the kidnapping operation. After saying goodbye to Risa and paying their respects at the Ginza memorial, the Special Region girls return to the Gate. Realizing the Empire's war with Japan will lead to its destruction, Piña makes plans to head back to the Capital to arrange peace talks between both sides.
11"Visitor"
Five months since the Gate's opening, the Alnus refugee camp has developed into a town and trading center for goods from Earth. At the Imperial capital, Piña introduces Kouji Sugawara, the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs' new ambassador to the Empire, to Lord Cicero, one of the most important nobles within the Empire's pro-war faction, and obtains his cooperation with the peace talks in exchange for the release of his nephew, who is currently in Japan's custody as a POW. Back in Alnus, Tuka keeps wandering the city looking for her father and refusing to accept the fact that he is already dead. As Itami and his friends discuss their concern for Tuka in a tavern, Kurokawa claims that they must make her face the truth, but Itami objects, certain that they can not be responsible for Tuka forever. Left alone with Rory, Itami keeps drinking with her until a Dark Elf woman by the name of Yao Haa Dushi appears and, mistaking Rory for a child, reprimands Itami for giving her alcohol. With her plans to spend the night with Itami ruined, an annoyed Rory mischievously plays along with the Dark Elf's misunderstanding, forcing Itami to flee. The Elf is unaware that Itami was one of the "Men in Green" she was looking for, whom she wants to ask for aid for her people, who are attacked by the Fire Dragon. The next day, as she prepares to visit the JSDF's base at Alnus, Itami heads towards the Imperial capital.
12"What Would Itami Do"
Yao's initial attempts to ask the JSDF for help fail, as most of the soldiers know little of the local language, and she is arrested by the Military Police after attacking several thugs who mistake her for a prostitute. Lelei, having improved her magic thanks to Earth's advanced scientific knowledge, is called by the JSDF to serve as Yao's interpreter. After learning her story, General Hazama tells Yao that he cannot help her, as her home, Schwartz Forest, is located in the Elbe Kingdom, which is outside the borders of the Empire. As the Japanese are currently in peace talks with the Empire, sending troops over their border would mean a declaration of war and reignite conflict. With Yao devastated at the news, some soldiers sympathize with her, and Lieutenant Akira Yanagida suggests that Yao should ask Itami for help. Elsewhere, Itami and his men deliver goods from Earth to Piña and Hamilton, as part of their plan to win over more nobles to seek peace with Japan. Before leaving, Itami gives Piña a Yaoi doujin translated by Bozes and Panache, which, unknown to him, contains newspaper clippings of his previous heroic actions. As Itami heads back to base hoping to achieve peace between both sides, Lelei narrates that the war is far from over.
13"The Banquet Begins"
In the Imperial Capital, a private party hosted by Piña is attended by a group of Senators and their families led by Lord Cicero, who, after seeing the 3rd Recon's weapons demonstrations, realizes the futility of fighting the Japanese and seeks to negotiate for peace. However, Crown Prince Zorzal, Piña's elder brother, learns of the meeting and rides with his entourage to confront the senators for treason. Itami's scouts spot the prince approaching, and the 3rd Recon helps the senators escape undetected before he arrives. At Akusho, the capital's red light district, Mari joins the JSDF team stationed there, using her training as a nurse to aid the locals who show up at the outpost. Meanwhile, Yao tries to learn about the people that are important to Itami from a local, while Itami, Shino and Akira stay at Pina's palace. Back at the Akusho outpost, the demi-human prostitutes warn Mari that they feel an "Earth-Shake" is coming. Recognizing it as a sign similar to how animals on Earth can detect earthquakes before they occur, Nyuutabaru, the commanding officer at the outpost, warns the soldiers in the Special Region to evacuate the civilians before the earthquake begins. 

14"The Imperial Capital Quake"
Piña invites Sugawara, Itami, Shino and Akira to meet with her father the Emperor in the Imperial Palace to advise them how to handle earthquakes. However, Zorzal also arrives to warn his father of another earthquake foretold by his slave Noriko, who is to Piña and the Japanese delegates' shock revealed as a Japanese citizen. Angered with Zorzal's cruel treatment of Noriko, Itami punches him and rescues the girl. Zorzal's bodyguards try to attack, only to be gunned down by Shino, and Itami and Shino torture Zorzal for information about other Japanese captives, only to be stopped by Tyuule, Zorzal's other slave. Sugawara warns the Emperor there will be repercussions if the kidnapped Japanese citizens are not returned to the Japanese before leaving, and the Japanese launch an air strike at the Imperial Senate building as a further message to make peace. While Tyuule treats Zorzal wounds, Zorzal younger brother, Diabo, learns their father wants to make Zorzal his heir, as he believes that he can easily control Zorzal from the shadows once he abdicates. Meanwhile, Noriko arrives at the JSDF Alnus base, hoping to return to Japan, unaware that her parents were killed during the Ginza incident. Elsewhere, Tuka continues to fruitlessly search for her father.
15"Tuka Luna Marceau"
At the Imperial capital, Diabo and Piña learn that Zorzal has been officially made heir to the throne and, aware of his father's plans, won't become his father's puppet. Unknown to them, Zorzal is being manipulated by Tyuule, who seeks revenge against the Empire and plans its destruction by the JSDF by having Noriko killed and Piña framed for it. At Alnus, Yanagida asks Itami to head to the Elbe Kingdom to kill the Fire Dragon, but Itami refuses as he won't endanger his soldier's lives. However, Tuka has gone insane and now believes Itami is her father after Yao forced her to face the fact that her father was killed by the Fire Dragon. Confronted, Yao reveals that she is desperate for Itami's help to save her people, even if it means hurting those close to him. Itami pretends to be Tuka's father for the time being, but Tuka still continues to slip further into madness. After having a talk with the disguised King Duran of Elbe, who is recuperating at Alnus, Itami finally decides to help Tuka confront and take revenge against the Fire Dragon, which will end her delusions. Rather than going to the Imperial capital with his men, Itami departs with Tuka, Rory, Lelei and Yao in a Humvee with supplies provided by Yanagida.
16"The Fire Dragon, Once More"
Delilah, the Warrior Bunny who works at the bar at Alnus refugee town, receives orders from her masters, the Formal Clan, that she is to assassinate Noriko, which, unknown to her, were actually forged by Tyuule, the former Queen of her tribe. When General Hazama learns of Itami's quest to Elbe, he forms a task force to help him fight the Fire Dragon, and Yanagida and King Duran make a deal to allow the JSDF to cross the Elbe Kingdom. Delilah attempts to kill Noriko fails when Yanagida discovers them, which ends with both of them injured fighting each other. The JSDF investigates the assassination attempt and, with help from the Formal Clan, learns the Formal Clan butler forged the letter under orders from Zorzal's faction, and to gain more information, one of Itami's soldiers, Furuta Hitoshi, goes undercover as a chef in the Capital, where he gains Zorzal's favor. Meanwhile, Itami's party finally reaches Yao's village. While Yao goes to greet her people, Itami and the others are surrounded by a group of Dark Elf guards, only for the Fire Dragon to appear. 

17"Decisive Battle"
After driving the Fire Dragon off and meeting the elders of the Dark Elves, Itami and his group heads to the Fire Dragon's nest in the mountains with a group of Dark Elf volunteers. With Rory guarding the entrance of the nest, Itami and his group install a fragmentation bomb beneath the Fire Dragon's nest using C4 and magic weapons lying around to kill the Fire Dragon by surprise. However, the Fire Dragon arrives and kills most of the Dark Elves. As the battle rages, Tuka finally accepts that her father is dead, and uses lighting magic, which ignites the C4, killing the Fire Dragon. As the survivors escape from the mountain, they find Rory heavily injured after fighting Giselle, a rival apostle. Giselle reveals she was the one that woke the Fire Dragon, which led to its rampage, as she was using the Fire Dragon's two hatchlings as help to capture Rory for her patron, the underworld goddess Hardy. Giselle's dragons chase after Itami and his group, only for the JSDF task force to arrive and kill the dragons, forcing Giselle to retreat.
18"The Magic City of Rondel"
Itami is punished for going AWOL fighting the Fire Dragon, but is right afterwards rewarded by various people for his heroic actions and given a new mission to scout for resources with Lelei, Rory, Tuka and Yao. The group heads to the Magic City of Rondel, where Lelei plans to hold a presentation to her fellow mages which, if successful, will gain her the rank of Master, and where they encounter Lelei's older sister Arpeggio and her mentor Mimoza La Mer. Meanwhile in the Imperial Capital, peace talks between Japan and the Empire officially begin, much to Zorzal's anger since the assassination attempt on Noriko and framing it on Pina have failed to derail it. As everyone celebrates the Fire Dragon's death, the Emperor is pleased to learn that Lelei, an Imperial citizen, was also involved in helping defeat the dragon. However, the Emperor suddenly falls ill after drinking wine, secretly poisoned under Tyuule's orders. 

19"Dangerous Sisters"
With the Emperor bedridden, Zorzal takes over the throne and declares his intent to avenge the Empire's humiliation by the Japanese. With the Imperial capital in curfew, the JSDF forces in Akusho are trapped and the Japanese Ambassadors put under house arrest. To Piña's anger, Zorzal has the pro-peace faction arrested and has his loyal followers planning to attack the Japanese with unconventional and unethical tactics, and her other brother Diabo has run away to seek help from other, superior forces to overthrow Zorzal. Meanwhile in Rondel, Mimoza reveals something interesting to Itami and the others about the Gate: Every few centuries or millenniums, the Gods of the Special Region would open a portal (the Gate) to another world at Alnus, through which the races of those worlds would come and settle in, explaining why they are many different types of races living here. When Arpeggio angrily learns that Lelei has outachieved her in any conceivable field (including finding a romantic interest with Itami), the sisters have a magic duel to settle their dispute. An assassin tries to kill Lelei at the end of the match but is eliminated by Grey. Grey and another Rose Knight, Shandy, reveal to Itami and his group that the assassin was sent by Zorzal due to his jealousy of Lelei's fame of defeating the Flame Dragon, and the two of them came to protect them under Piña's orders. Rather than stay and fight, however, Itami decides that it's best they run away from the assassins.
20"Lover"
As Itami and his group continue to evade Zorzal's killers, Zorzal's secret police continue to arrest the pro-peace faction for treason throughout the capital. Despite this, the Japanese are ordered by their government to not get involved, including refusing sanctuary for the pro-peace faction. Marquess Casel seeks refuge with the Thierry Family, only for the Oprichnina to attack their home, forcing their daughter Sherry to help Casel escape while her parents sacrifice themselves to stop them. Sherry and Casel head to the Jade Palace, which has become the Japanese embassy, to seek asylum, as the palace is under the Rose Knights' protection and a treaty prevents the Empire from setting foot there. Despite Sherry hoping Sugawara, whom she sees as her future husband, to help them, Sugawara sticks to his country's orders to not get involved. However, when the Oprichnina arrive and arrest Casel and Sherry, Sugawara changes his mind and takes Sherry under his custody, thus starting a brutal battle between the Rose Knights and the Oprichnina. Despite what happened, Vice-Minister Shirayuri allows it and contacts her government.
21"Deadline"
The Rose Knights manage to repel the Oprichnina and free Senator Casel, but this leads to an escalation of tension between Japan and the Empire. Minister Kanou and other members of the government suggest to evacuate the Japanese delegation from the Jade Palace, but Prime Minister Morita refuses to give the green light, since representatives from other nations and the media are currently visiting the Special Region and the Alnus camp, so a demonstration of force or having no control of the situation could have bad diplomatic consequences for Japan. However, things turn bad rapidly when Zorzal has Piña under arrest for her refusal to order the Rose Knights to let his soldiers enter the palace and orders his army to put the embassy under siege, which finally drives Morita into authorizing the JSDF's deployment to evacuate the ambassadors and political refugees. Meanwhile in Rondel, Itami and the others manage to neutralize another assassination attempt against them, and prepare a plan to capture the Piper, the leader of the assassins sent to kill them.
22"The Imperial Princess in Slave's Clothing"
The Imperial Army attempts to break through the embassy are repelled by the Rose Knights, but with the massive difference in numbers it's just a matter of time until the Jade Palace's falls. Meanwhile, in Rondel, Shandy discovers that the Piper is planning another assassination attempt against Lelei, so Itami and the others prepare themselves to stop him. As expected, during Lelei's presentation, two more assassins try to kill her, but they're both thwarted by Itami and the spectators. However, at the final moment Shandy tries to stab Lelei, but is saved thanks to the armor under her dress. Interrogated about her betrayal, Shandy reveals that the Piper forced her to kill Lelei in order to save Piña, who has been formally accused of high treason. Characterisation of mango pectin extracted via microwave
Abstract
This study investigates the viability of microwave-assisted extraction as an alternative to traditional acid extraction for obtaining pectin from mango peel, a by-product of mango processing. Utilising microwave technology presents a more energy-efficient and less chemically intensive method for pectin extraction, aligning with the sustainability goals of the UN. Keitt mangoes were chosen for this study due to high waste valorising potential. Comparison of the extraction methods, both with multiple reaction conditions tested, showed that microwave extraction at 140⁰c provided a pectin with the most desirable properties, which was the best compromise of degree of esterification (DE) and yield (42.7322% and 0.2071g respectively). Further analysis assessed the quality of the extracted pectin against JEFCA standards through measurements of purity parameters, such as loss on drying and nitrogen content. While the study demonstrated that the pectin could yield desirable properties, it fell short in some of the purity parameters, making the resultant pectin’s applicability in the food industry limited by its compositional properties. However, it’s potential in medicinal application, with it being a low methoxy pectin (LMP) and the plausible presence of calcium pectinate (CaP) salts, warrants further investigation. In conclusion, while microwave-assisted extraction offers a viable, environmentally friendly method for pectin extraction , achieving commercial viability requires addressing the purity and composition challenges, with future research being to aim for optimisation of extraction conditions and exploring the full range of possible applications for the extracted pectin, considering its unique properties.     
Introduction
The large amount of food waste worldwide has a massive impact the raw materials  in food production, creating a global environmental and social imbalance that affect third world countries the most[1]. In the UK alone, 9.5 million tonnes of food waste is produced, not only releasing 36 million tonnes of CO2 emission equivalents, but also costing the government £19 billion[2]. It does not help that 70% of this waste could have been eaten, in a world where up to 783 million people have limited access to food[3]. This also does not fall in line with the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target 12.3 (‘By 2030 halve per capita global food waste… and reduce food losses along production and supply chains, including post-harvest losses’) where it has only reduced by 13.2% globally[4], and with less than 7 years left of the SDGs implementation, drastic changes must happen in the near future in order to reach this target.
Approximately 14% of food produced is lost between harvest and retail[5], and in the case of fruits this will be due to either how it is processed before being put on retail, purposely thrown away due to the products aesthetics or it is spoiling before reaching retail[6]. Processed fruit generates 2 types of waste: liquid waste, as a result of juicing and water used to wash the fruit, and solid waste, for example the peel that equates to around 15 to 60% of the solid waste[7]. The solid fruit waste can be valorised by extracting compounds that can be used in multiple industries, e.g. semisolids, i.e. creams or ointments, with oils extracted from the seed[8].
Mangoes are an interesting fruit with high solid waste valorising potential; there are many cultivars of mangoes harvested around the world, such as Alphonso from India and Tommy Atkins from the United States of America. They are a fruit growing in popularity, with 43,000 tonnes being imported into the UK in 2022[9]. The by-products of mango processing totals 35-60% of the weight of the fruit (peel, kernel, seed)[10], and contains several extractable compounds, including antioxidants such as xanthone C-glycosides[11] and dietary fibres[12]. With each variety of mango having different amounts of extractable compounds, specific species can be exploited for valorisation in different industries. One extractable compound, with potential use in multiple industries, that all mangoes contain a large amount is pectin.
Pectin is a polysaccharide used by plants for cell wall adhesion[13] and has influences in other parts of  plants morphogenesis such as root elongation[14]. It is a family of galacturonic acids derived from the monomer uronic acid; with the cell walls of mango peel containing approximately 52% uronic acid[15], there is large prospects for valorising the peel for galacturonic acids, with potential to compete with the main sources of commercially available pectin, which are citrus peel, apple pomace and sugar beet pulp[16].The residues of homogalacturonan (HG) can be methylated on C6 or acetylated on O2 or O3 on the carbohydrate ring to form esters[17]; some of the C6 esters can be unmethylated, leaving a negative charge, which can interact with calcium ions that helps support the adhesion of pectin chains and gelatinisation, dubbed the ‘egg-box’ model[18]. This gelling effect caused by the HG-calcium ion interactions means that when extracted from the peels, pectin has applications in the food industry as a thickening agent in jams, jellies, and milk products[19], making it a non-meat alternative to gelatine for the diets of people who choose to, e.g. vegetarians and vegans, or cannot consume specific meat products, such as Muslims. It can also be used in medicine to coat drugs and formulate capsules that are pH dependent for delivery to specific parts of the body[20]. 
Pectin extraction has been done industrially since the late 20th century via acid stewing, but it is not very efficient;. the vat required to heat up the water and maintain the temperature for several hours requires a lot of energy[22], in addition to the acid that can potentially produce unwanted byproducts, thus decreasing the yield and quality of the pectin that can be extracted. Microwave technology can breakdown the mango peel without the need for acid, as well as requiring less energy to heat the mango[22], making it a viable method replacement of acid extraction. Microwave-assisted extraction has been researched on and trialled since 2015[23], with one of the more noteworthy papers looks at a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of extracted pectin from citrus peel at pilot scale[22]. The first aim of this study is to show a comparison between acid and microwave-assisted extraction, showing that microwave technology is a viable alternative to the traditional method. A second aim of this study is to compare the results obtained from this research to the results from this paper[22] and suggest if mango peel is viable competitor of citrus peel for pectin extraction. This comparison will be done on a larger batch of pectin that will be extracted via the conditions determined to be the best from the comparison of methods and conditions.
In 2009, the FAO published a pectin characterisation tests and purity parameters in the JEFCA Monographs[23], with purity tests including loss on drying, galacturonic acid contents and nitrogen contents, setting requirements to ensure safety for human consumption. While at a laboratory-scale study, the parameters cannot be tested in the required method due to the amount of pectin needed being unable to be made in a small timescale , approximations of some can be found through other methods that require much less yield. The final aim of this study is to obtain approximate purity values of parameters that can be tested on the larger batch of pectin, and to propose if a move to a larger scale of research is needed. 
Methods
Materials                                                                                                                                                    Keitt mangoes, from Brazil, were sourced from a local supermarket and processed to acquire the peel via a sharp knife, with the flesh removed with a  stainless steel spoon. From 10 mangoes, 817g of peel was obtained.
All chemicals used, i.e. ethanol, HCl, H2SO4 and phenolphthalein, were purchased from Fischer Chemicals and used without further purification. 
Pectin extraction and purification                                                                                                                                                                        Pectin extraction was attempted using the traditional method (acid stewing) and microwave-assisted extraction. The traditional method consisted of  a 1hr reflux on 10g of peel and aqueous HCl in 4 different conditions; temperatures of 85⁰c and 100⁰c, and peel to solvent ratios (p:s) of 1:10 (0.03M HCl) and 1:30 (0.01M HCl) were both tested, with the mango filtered out after the hour. The microwave-assisted extraction uses a CEM MARS 6 extraction system, in which 5g of peel and 50ml of water is put into each easy prep plus vessel with a stirrer flea. 4 different temperatures were tested (100⁰c, 120⁰c, 140⁰c, and 160⁰c), with the power set to 600W. Both methods resulted with aqueous solutions containing pectin. Pectin was isolated from the solution with the addition of excess ethanol (c.a. 2.5:1 ratio of ethanol to water) under rapid stirring for 20 minutes, with the solution left overnight for maximum precipitation. Centrifugation is then needed for further isolation, which was done with a Thermo Megafuge Centrifuge at 3900rpm for 20 minutes (acceleration value at 9 and deceleration value at 3), with falcon tubes containing 40ml of a 5:3 ratio of solution to ethanol. The resultant pectin pellet was extracted and purified by boiling in excess ethanol for 15 minutes before hot filtering with a sinter funnel to obtain an off-white solid. The solid is put into the freezer for 4 hours before undergoing freeze-drying to obtain the final product[10].                              
Characterisation of Pectin
Degrees of Esterification (DE) using infrared spectroscopy (IR)                                                                  Attenuated total reflectance IR (ATR-IR) was achieved using a Perkin Elmer Spectrum 400 IR. The spectra was taken at a range of 4000cm-1 to 650cm-1, with a blank background reading. After the spectra is produced, it is converted to absorbance, from transmittance, and with the areas of the ester and acid peaks calculated (c.a. 1750cm-1 and 1600cm-1 respectively), the DE is determined as a percentage of the ester peak against the total area.
Degrees of Esterification via titration (DEt)                                                                                            500mg is moistened with 2ml of ethanol before being dissolved in 100ml of deionised water. 5 drops of phenolphthalein is added and was titrated with 0.5M NaOH (denoted as initial titre). Thereafter 10ml of 0.5M NaOH was added and mixed vigorously, with the solution allowed to stand for 15 minutes. 10ml of 0.5 HCl was added after, and the solution was shaken until the pink colour disappeared. 5 drops of phenolphthalein was added to the solution and it was titrated again with 0.5M NaOH to a faint pink colour persisted after shaking (end point). This was recorded as the final titre. The DEt was calculated with the following equation: DEt (%) = (final titre)/(initial titre+final titre)×100[25]. 
Galacturonic acid contents                                                                                                                     100mg of pectin (denoted as W) is mixed with 1ml of 72% H2SO4 and subjected to shaking in a water bath (40⁰c), being stirred every 5 to 10 minutes for 2 hours with a glass stirring rod. Thereafter, 28 ml of deionised water is added to the mixture, before autoclaved for 1 hour at 121⁰c. The resulting hydrolysed sample is filtered through a sinter funnel, and the liquid is further filtered through a RC 0.22µm filter dish before subjected for galacturonic acid analysis via HPLC[26].
Loss on drying                                                                                                                                                             25mg of the sample in a sample vial is placed in a biomass drying oven at 105⁰c for 2 hours. After leaving to cool until the sample reaches room temperature, the mass is recorded after and the difference is measured as a percentage.
Nitrogen contents                                                                                                                                            The percentage of nitrogen is obtained using CHN analysis with a Thermo Flash CHNS-O, and is given as a percentage.
Total insolubles                                                                                                                                    After filtration of the sample for galacturonic acid analysis, the mass of the sinter funnel with the hydrolysed solid is measured (denoted as W0). The solid is washed with deionised water before the sinter funnel is placed in a biomass drying oven for 1 hour at 105⁰c. The mass of the sinter funnel with the dried solid is measured (denoted as W1). The calculation can be performed with the equation:  Insoluble pectin (%) = (W1- W0)/W×100[26].

Determination of the best method and condition
The degrees of esterification obtained from acid reflux conditions ranged from 30.82% to 37.05%, in comparison to microwave conditions which range from 32.09% to 43.16%. DE is defined as a percentage of the preservation of the esterified carboxyl bonds in comparison to the total amount of carboxyl bonds in pectin[27]. It is a measurement of pectin quality that is easily influenced by the extraction conditions, and as it can be determined quickly through IR, it makes for an ideal parameter to compare the two methods, and the different conditions for each of them. Pectin can be classed as either high methoxy pectin (HMP), where the DE is greater than 50%, or low methoxy pectin (LMP), in which DE is less than 50%. LMP’s are seen as more valuable due to gelation able to be achieved with calcium ions at a wider range of pH in comparison to HMP, which require an environment with high sugar content[27]; however a pectin with a low DE tends to be more brittle due to the dependency on calcium ions to maintain the gelation[28]. From Table 1, it can be concluded that microwave extraction at 140⁰c performed the best of any of the conditions tested as it shows a balance between DE and yield; the DE is low enough to meet the LMP threshold, but not too low that if left to form a gel, it is not too brittle, and the yield obtained is much larger than most of the other tested conditions. This was enough justification that the batch of pectin to be further characterised was extracted with this method and condition. It was interesting to observe that the highest yield, which was from acid reflux at 85⁰c and a peel to solvent ratio of 1:30, was a 35% increase to what was recorded with the microwave at 140⁰c; an unexcepted result as it has been recorded that at more optimal conditions, microwave-assisted extraction should have a greater yield recorded in comparison to acid stewing[10, 22]. This led to a side experiment, in which 2 more microwave reactions at 140⁰c took place with the same amount of mango peel and 50ml of 0.01M HCl and H2SO4 solution instead of water. Sulphuric acid is tested as it is another acid that can be used in acid extraction[29].

Microwave extraction with acid solution                                                                                                            The aim of this was only to see whether the replacement of water for acid solution would have an effect on the yield or DE. The data in Table 2 shows that the addition of acid had increased DE to 54.7417% and 50.6012%, but decreased yield by approximately 64% and 75% for H2SO4 and HCl respectively. The increase in DE indicates that the use of acid solution in the microwave vessels compared to deionised water aids in the preservation of the esterified carboxyl groups; this may have occurred as under acidic conditions, the ester bonds are less likely to hydrolyse compared to the glycosidic bonds that are located in the main pectic polysaccharide chain, and the microwave more likely enhances this effect with more even energy distribution in comparison to acid stewing. The decrease in yield could also have happened for the same reason, in which the combination of both is favoured for glycosidic bond hydrolysis; this leads to higher amounts of premature pectin chain termination, which is more solubilised in the acidic conditions and are not so easily recovered in the purification process. A higher DE for H2SO4 comes from the way the sulphate ions interact with the pectin environment, affecting the solubility and stability of the extractable polysaccharide in a way that aids the release from the peel. The reason that H2SO4 also recorded a higher yield than HCl is that it is a diprotic acid[30] instead of a monoprotic acid; the donation of 1 more proton per molecule, and the accumulation of these extra protons lead to more effective protonation of the ester linkages, which promotes hydrolysis of pectin to more extractable fragments. While these results are noteworthy, this experiment was to only see what effect the combination of acid solution and microwave technology would do for pectin extraction, and has no bearing on the overall conclusion of this report.

Degree of Esterification                                                                                                         The DE, determined via IR, was recorded at 41.7780%, which is similar to what was observed with the result from Table 1, showing consistency with analytical precision. While IR is a quick method to obtain a DE value, there are a few limitations. an example is baseline drift, in which the line either side of the peak does not return to absolute 0, but will instead be shown as an elevated baseline. This can come across due to sample characteristics or atmospheric absorption, and affect the DE as a true value cannot be determined. Titrimetry is another method of DE determination, and while it is a more versatile method with less sensitivity to sample conditions than IR, it still has limitations, such as endpoint determination. The combination of both methods can be used for cross verification of results,  and as similar values are recorded, then there is an increase in the confidence that the true DE value is within the range of both values (41.7780 – 46.1034%). Comparing this to what was attained from citrus peel in Tom et al’s paper[22] (72.8%), both have a vast difference in esterification, and are clearly meant for different applications, with the citrus restricted to high-sugar jams and jellies, as well as less potential uses in medicine[28].
Loss on drying                                                                                                                                Loss on drying was found to be at 11.0336%, which meets the threshold of 12% maximum loss of sample mass. This primarily shows that the pectin has a desirable quality and integrity that is crucial for applications in the food industry, due to excessive moisture in pectin that could lead to microbial growth or spoilage, and decreasing shelf life. The adherence of the pectin batch to the JEFCA requirements is indicative of the efficacy of the purification process, as it shows that the use of the freeze-dryer in the drying stage is removing the desired amount of moisture without overly dehydrating the pectin, which could potentially compromise quality and functionality. Again comparing this to the results in the LCA paper (8.98%), the difference shows that process that they undertook was more effective in drying out excess moisture out of the pectin that what was done here, which would result in a longer shelf life than the mango pectin.
Total insolubles                                                                                                                             The upper limit for total insoluble is 3%, and as can be seen in Table 3, the recorded value (4.0527%) is above the limit. This could be due to the formation of calcium pectinate (CaP) salts; With the egg-box model of pectin and calcium interactions, this facilitates the cross-linking that is formed between the ions and the HG chains, forming a three-dimensional structure. This forms a CaP gel[31], and with changes to the conditions, in time this will crystalise to form an insoluble salt. The presence of this salt will contribute to the total weight of the insoluble fraction. The contrast between this result and what was obtained in Tom et al’s paper[22] (0.29%), despite it only being approximately 3.7%, is quite significant, as one is far below the threshold and the other is far above it, showing a vast difference in purity. While the presence of CaP is not ideal for applications in the food industry, there has been research for use of these salts in medicine, for example in colonic drug delivery with silica-coated beads[32], in which the aim would be to exploit the conditions in the gastrointestinal tract to allow for conditioned release of drugs, showing that there is still potential use for this sample for a different application despite not meeting the JEFCA requirement.
Nitrogen content                                                                                                                                       The nitrogen content that was recorded (0.58%) falls well within the 2.5% maximum threshold from the JEFCA requirements. This shows that the pectin chains have a high level of purity, with little nitrogen-containing compounds present. Nitrogen contents mainly test for two types of compounds, one type being protein insolubles; while most proteins would be removed in the extraction and purification process, it is feasible that not all would be removed. These are considered impurities, and can affect the gelling properties of the pectin. The other type of nitrogen-containing compound that could be present are alkaloids. These are naturally occurring toxic amines that are produced by plants as a defence mechanism, and consumption of these amines can lead to disruption in multiple parts of the body, such as the central nervous system[33]. It is important to test for nitrogen contents as  a result over the threshold means a possibility of the presence of alkaloids, making it unsafe for food and medicinal applications.

Galacturonic Acid Content                                                                                                                    From HPLC, it was determined that the content of galacturonic acid was 37.2361%. This is significantly lower than the minimum requirement set by JEFCA (>65%), and what was obtained in Tom et al paper on citrus fruit (72.3%). A reason for this could be the raw material that was used, in which Keitt mangoes may have inherently low levels of galacturonic acid content; the results suggests this as a high presence of other sugars can be seen; 23.5518% of the sample is the cellulose, which can be extracted and used as a dietary fibre[34]. 27.9798% of the contents are sugars that are present in hemicellulose (Fructose & Mannose) and ‘hairy’ pectin (Xylose, Rhamnose & Arabinose). Hemicellulose are matrix polysaccharides that form hydrogen bonds to cellulose microfibrils[35] to help strengthen the cell wall. They can be formed by different monosaccharides, and can also be used as a dietary fibre[36]. ‘Hairy’ pectin is a region of the chain that has branching of other monosaccharides, as shown in Figure 3. This can disrupt the gelling behaviour of the pectin as they can interfere with the ‘egg-box’ interactions of calcium ions and the ‘smooth’ galacturonic acid pectin region. Levoglucosan is a product of cellulose pyrolysis[37], whereas the results denoted as ‘Others’ in Table 4 are not, they are degradation products of galacturonic acids; these show that the conditions the microwave produce have an unwanted side effect of breaking down polysaccharide chains, which can reduce purity of the sample and the yield obtained. The presence of all of these products at such a high proportion, in comparison to how little galacturonic acid there is in the sample shows a high level of impurity that no other JEFCA parameter has been able to measure, and presents the case that it is not ready to move to higher scale research.
Yield                                                                                                                                              0.977g of pectin was extracted from 60g of Keitt mango peel, equating to a yield of 1.62%. Comparing to the literature, in 2016 paper by Avtar et al [10], a dry weight yield of 11.63% from 20g of dried mango peel, and in the LCA paper, 150g of pectin was extracted from 3kg of citrus peel, which reflects an extraction efficiency of 5%. What must be noted is that the pectin from this research was obtained through undried mango peel, which impacts how much can be extracted due to the high moisture content of fresh peel, which can vary between ~59 to ~69% of mango cultivars[38]. Based on these moisture numbers, a theoretical yield from dry peel can be obtained using the mean moisture content (64%) by finding the dry mass of the fresh peel and obtaining a yield percentage based on that; using this, the dry peel mass would be 21.6g (60g×0.36=21.6g), meaning the percentage would have been 4.61%. This is quite comparable to the citrus peel, showing a minor decrease, but as that was done with a much larger amounts of peel, a downscaled extraction could increase yield percentage difference. What this does is bring up the question of whether it is worth it to valorise Keitt mango peel for pectin as the primary source, or to obtain it as a side product, for applications in the food industry. Looking at the HPLC results, 23.55% of the 0.977g of pectin was actually cellulose as an unintended side product; cellulose extraction efficiency of mango peel has been recorded at 44.6%[39], and with this it seems that it would be better to have cellulose as the main extraction product of Keitt mango peel, and to see whether pectin can be extracted as a side product.


Conclusion
The use of microwaves as a means to extract pectin from mango peel is a viable alternative and potential replacement of the traditional acid extraction method, with more optimal conditions providing the best compromise between DE and yield (42.7322% and 0.2071g respectively), showing the potential of microwave technology for valorisation of food wastes for biobased chemicals and materials. The data also shows that the source is not be a viable competitor of some of the main sources of pectin, such as citrus peel, but there is potential to compete with other LMP sources; this would need more research to optimise as the data obtained from the research also shows that using Keitt mango peel as a source of pectin for applications in the food industry is not a viable source, as some of the purity parameters  that JEFCA have set to regulate commercial pectin production (galacturonic acid contents and total insolubles) have not been met. There might be potential use for the pectin for medicinal uses instead, with some of the total insolubles potentially being CaP salts. However further research would need to occur to confirm the presence of the salts.

abstract

Twin boundaries have been exploited to stabilize ultrafine grains and improve the mechanical properties of nanomaterials. The production of twin boundaries and nanotwins is however prohibitively challenging in carbide ceramics. Using scanning transmission electron microscopes as a unique platform for atomic-scale structure engineering, we demonstrate that twin platelets could be produced in carbides by engineering antisite defects.
Antisite defects at metal sites in various layered ternary carbides are collectively and controllably generated and the metal elements are homogenized by electron irradiation, which transforms the twin-like lamellae into nanotwin platelets. Accompanying the chemical homogenization, α-Ti3AlC2 transforms to unconventional β-Ti3AlC2.
The chemical homogeneity and the width of the twin platelets can be tuned by the dose and energy of bombarding electrons. Chemically homogenized nanotwins can boost the hardness by ~45%. Our results provide a new way to produce ultrathin (<5 nm) nanotwin platelets in scientifically and technologically important carbide materials and showcase the feasibility of defect engineering by an angstrom-sized electron probe.
Nanotwinned structures are energetically more stable than normal nanograins with comparable grain sizes as the excess energy of a coherent twin boundary is roughly ten times lower than that of normal grain boundaries . Nanotwinning has thus been used to produce stable ultrafine grains (<5 nm) in metals, e.g.
Cu and Ti 3 alloys, and ceramics, e.g. diamonds and cubic BN . The latter generally requires extreme environments such as high pressure and high temperature due to the strong covalent bonds. Interestingly, atomically thin twin-like lamellae naturally exist in ternary layered carbide ceramics, Mn+1ACn phases, which have the merits of both metals and ceramics and hold promise for applications in high-temperature foil bearings, heating elements, electrical contacts, coatings on nuclear materials, etc .
In these unique structures, A (A group elements, mainly Al) layers structurally act as mirror planes of the Mn+1Cn slabs (Fig. ), where M is a transition metal element. The metallic M-A bonding in Mn+1ACn phases is significantly weaker than the ionic and covalent M-C bonding . The twin-like interfaces therefore have no strengthening or hardening effect in Mn+1ACn phases, yet are the Achilles' heel of these structures, where the deformation and delamination occur first .
It has been expected that the twin-like interfaces could be used to boost the mechanical properties if we can find a way to diminish the chemical anisotropy near the interface. There are two possible routes to achieve this. One may remove A-layers from the structure by chemical etching or heat treatment.
The former results in MXenes and weaker structures because of the intercalation of atoms like O, F, H or even molecules. The latter method can produce twins but the process is uncontrollable (Fig. ). Another way is to chemically homogenize M and A without destroying the mirrored structures. Heat treatment has been used to tune the distribution of constituent elements in twins , but is inapplicable for Mn+1ACn phases because of phase decompositions .
We thus turned to engineer the antisite defects with the irradiation of energetic particles. In Mn+1ACn phases, antisite defects MA and AM (MA: M at A sites or AM: A at M sites ) could form with the bombardment of energetic particles with low radiation fluence (~0.2 dpa) due to their relatively low formation energy (2~3 eV for Ti3AlC2 ) compared to other point-defect pairs (6~8 eV).
The accumulation of antisite defects could lead to the transformation of hexagonal Mn+1AXn to face-centered-cubic (Mn+1A)Xn with large amounts of nanotwins . However, due to the large beam size and poor controllability of beam position, the most used heavy ion irradiation is infeasible to spatially engineer the defects at nanometer or smaller scale, which requires atomicscale atom manipulation.
With remarkable improvements in spatial resolution and electron-probe controllability , scanning transmission electron microscopes become a new platform to manipulate atoms , cations and vacancies , trigger phase transformations and induce the movement of grain and phase boundaries. Here, we demonstrate that angstrom-sized electron probes can work as an effective stimulator for the solid-state chemical homogenization in various Mn+1ACn phases to produce chemically homogenized twins.
The three-layer-thick titanium carbide lamellae in Ti3AlC2 are mirrored with respect to the Al-layers (Fig. ). Crystallographically, there are two sites for Al at the twinlike plane of titanium carbide lamellae, which leads to two polytypes, i.e. α-Ti3AlC2 (Fig. ) and β-Ti3AlC2 (Fig. ). The latter has been assumed to exist for decades but never conclusively confirmed in experiments before.
In the high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images, the contrast is in proportion to (the average of for all the atoms in the column along the projection direction), where Z is the atomic number and n≈2. The atomic columns with high and low intensities in Fig. ,g are Ti-layers and Al-layers, respectively.
Comparing the atomic positions in Al-layers and Ti-layers (green rectangles) in [12 10]-images with the structural model (Fig. ) suggests that Ti3AlC2 in (d) and (e) takes the α-and β-configurations, respectively. The [101 0]-images of the two polytypes (Fig. ) agree well with the model (Fig. ). We found that the intensity of Al-layers increases with the accumulation of electron doses along the two zone axes (Fig. ,h,f,i, Video S1 and S2), indicating certain amounts of Ti atoms run into Al-layers.
As the irradiation dose accumulates to ~4 × 10 7 e -/Å 2 , the intensity of Al-layers reaches ~83% of the intensity of Ti-layers (inset in Fig. ). From Fig. , the composition of Ti-layers and Al-layers was estimated to be Ti0.8Al0.2 and Al0.4Ti0.6, respectively. It is well-established that HAADF-STEM has a depth of field Δz=λ/α 2 (α is the convergence semi-angle) .
The structural features within Δz are in-focus and dominate the contrast in the images. The nearly identical intensity of Ti-layers and Al-layers in a region of ~20 nm in thickness imaged with 30 mrad (Δz=2.2 nm), 20 mrad (Δz=4.9 nm) and 10 mrad (Δz=19.6 nm) in Fig. suggests that the repartitioning is not limited to the regions near the surface, but throughout the sample, which is corroborated by the atomic-scale mapping of Ti-K and Al-K signals via energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy (Fig. ), where the number of Ti atoms in Al-layers gradually increases, while accordingly that of Al atoms in Al-layers decreases to the same level of Ti-layers.
As shown in Fig. , EDX simulations using quantum excitation of phonon multislice suggest that Al K-edge is more delocalized than that of Ti K-edge, which seemly forms a continuous line instead of atomically resolved individual columns. The core-shell electrons of light elements are weakly bound to their nuclei as compared to heavy elements.
As a consequence, light elements exhibit a rather delocalized ionization potential for X-ray generation . But the homogenization of Al is still evident in Fig. . Irradiation-induced repartitioning also occurs in other Alcontaining MAX phases, e.g. Ti2AlC (Video S3, S4) and Nb4AlC3 (Fig. ). It is noted that there is no noticeable repartitioning in Nb2SC (Fig. ), which might be due to the remarkably high formation energy (8.6 eV) of M/A antisite defects compared to Alcontaining MAX phases (2~3 eV) like Ti3AlC2, Ti2AlC, Nb2AlC and Nb4AlC3 (Table ).
The repartitioning is readily controllable by electron dose and energy of the impinging electrons (Fig. ). The number of Ti atoms redistributed into Al-layers monotonically scales with the dose accumulation. The trends revealed by EDX quantification and semi-quantitative analysis of HAADF-STEM images are pretty consistent, and monitoring the intensity change in HAADF-STEM images directly could give a fairly good estimate of the process in practice.
The elemental process of the repartitioning is the knock-on of Ti, Al and C atoms. Ab-initio molecular dynamics simulation suggests that Ti/Al and C atoms in defectfree Ti3AlC2 need ~13 eV and ~5 eV to be knocked out (Fig. , Video S5, Table ), which could be sufficiently supplied by the energy transfer from the impinging electrons to Ti3AlC2 at 300 kV, where Ti, Al and C atoms can be powered with 17.8 eV, 31.6 eV and 70.9 eV, respectively.
In real electron-atom interaction, the atoms on the surface are the easiest and earliest to be knocked out, which is known as sputtering . Depending on the surface plane, the energy needed by Ti, Al and C to be sputtered is 2~6 eV (Table ), which could be easily met by the energy transfer from 200 kV electrons to those atoms, the maximum of which is 11.0 eV for Ti, 19.4 eV for Al and 43.7 eV for C. The sputtering of constituent atoms on the surface creates defects, which will significantly lower the displacement threshold energy of the atoms near the surface and result in a cascade effect.
Therefore Ti/Al antisite defects were observed at 200 kV (Fig. ), despite that the maximum energy Ti could obtain from impinging electrons is slightly lower than the threshold calculated with the defect-free model, 11.0 eV vs. 13.0 eV. Actually, Ti atoms can even be knocked out at 80 kV . The lower energy the incident electrons have, the less energy can be transferred to the atoms within the sample, and the fewer atoms could be powered to the energy threshold needed to move out of their original crystal sites.
Therefore, it takes a higher electron dose at 200 kV (black spheres in Fig. ) than 300 kV (green spheres in Fig. ) to achieve the same level of atomic repartition. At 200 kV, Ti atoms in Al-layers approach the limit of 75% with a dose of ~4.7 × 10 8 e -/Å 2 , where nearly complete homogenization is attained.
With the complete homogenization of Ti and Al, the structure becomes nanotwins. The twin platelets are equivalent to the ∑ 3 111 twin lamellae in a face-centered cubic structure. With further irradiation, the adjacent twin platelets could be merged into a thicker one, e.g. ~3 nm in Fig. . Carbon atoms are much easier to be knocked out considering the low displacement threshold energy (~5 eV) and high kinetic energy (~71 eV at 300 kV) they can get from the impinging electrons.
But we were unable to see where the displaced C atoms stay in HAADF-STEM images (Fig. ) due to the well-known intrinsic limitation of this imaging modality. Alternatively, we turned to four-dimensional (4D) STEM ptychographic phase imaging, which has remarkable light-element sensitivity . C columns are unequivocally resolved in the phase image (black arrows in Fig. ).
The remarkably inhomogeneous intensities of the C-layers marked by black solid arrows suggest that some displaced C atoms stay at the interstitial sites of carbide lamellae. More importantly, some displaced C atoms move to the space between Al-layers and Ti-layers (black hollow arrows in Fig. ). Interestingly, the homogenization of C is significantly slower than that of Ti and Al, which might be due to the highly movable nature of C (Video S5).
The time resolution of the current microscope is at the scale of microseconds, which is too long to be able to reveal the dynamical repartitioning process and shed insights on the counterintuitive repartitioning behavior of C. Accompanying the repartitioning of constituent atoms, α-polytype (Fig. ) transforms into β-polytype (Fig. ,h,f,i).
We observed that and β-polytypes coexist between nanotwins and their pristine counterparts, exhibiting line-like contrasts in the HAADF-STEM images (Fig. ). The line profile of the line-like layer (transition region in Fig. ) shows two different periodicities, d1=0.28 and d2=0.1 nm (Fig. ). The former corresponds to the distance between the Al columns in α-or β-polytype, while the latter is the space of Al columns between α-and β-polytype (Fig. ).
The pairs with 0.1 nm distance are clearly resolved in the ptychographic phase image (green arrows in Fig. ). The β-polytype is metastable and has never been synthesized in experiments before . However, it gradually becomes thermodynamically more favorable than the most common -polytype with the formation of TiAl and AlTi antisite defects (Fig. ).
Specifically, the value of Eβ-Eα becomes negative when 32~48% (~40% on average) Al in Al-layers are replaced by Ti, suggesting α-to-β transition may occur if 32~48% TiAl forms in Al-layers, which is remarkably consistent with the experiments where we observed that β-polytype forms when ~30% Al was replaced by Ti (Fig. ).
To elucidate the stabilization mechanism of β-polytype, we closely inspected the electron structures via partial density of states (pDOS, Fig. ). In the energy range from -5 eV to the Fermi energy (EF), Ti 3d electrons are dominant compared to Al and C. For -polytype, the density of states of antisite (aTi) and neighboring Ti (sTi) at EF are 1.47 a.u. and 0.46 a.u., respectively.
The significant difference in the density of states between aTi and sTi suggests that breaking Ti-C bonds may render considerable amounts of 3d electrons in -polytype unsaturated. While in β-polytype, the density of states of aTi and sTi at EF are close (0.89 a.u vs. 0.88 a.u) and the peaks at -0.40~-0.10
eV are largely overlapped, indicating that orbital hybridization occurs between aTi and sTi, which reduces the unsaturated 3d electrons. We thus speculated that the pronounced difference in electronic structures dictates the relative stability of and βpolytype. To gain more insights into this issue, the bonding states of aTi, aAl, sTi and C atoms were calculated via the crystal orbital Hamilton population (COHP) curves .
As can be seen in Fig. , nonbonding states of aTi prevail in the highest occupied bands close to EF in -polytype, while β-polytype is massively characterized by aTi-sTi and aTi-aAl bonding interactions. Integrated COHP of β is more negative than that of  for orbitals (Table ), confirming stronger bonding interactions in β, which makes β-polytype more stable.
Angstrom-sized electron probes can serve not only as a markedly coherent "light source" for advanced real-space imaging but also as a highly controllable power source for atoms to jump out of their potential valley. Using the state-of-the-art transmission electron microscope, we homogenized M and Al elements in various Mn+1AlCn and produced ultrathin (<5 nm) carbide nanotwin platelets.
The homogenization process is readily controllable by electron dose and energy. Accompanying the homogenization, the unconventional β-polytype forms in Ti3AlC2. More importantly, the irradiated region could dilate ~3.0% along the c-axis (Fig. ), contract by 0.6% along the aaxis and expand by ~1.9% in volume.
The slight volumetric expansion exerts compressive stress on the untransformed region. In addition, chemical homogenization removes the bonding anisotropy of Ti3AlC2 and turns the weak twin-like interface into strong twin boundaries of (Ti,Al)3C2. We speculate that these two factors have positive effects on mechanical properties.
As a proof-of-concept study, we irradiated Ti3AlC2 bulk sample (Fig. ) and measured the micro-hardness. Ti and Al were nearly completely homogenized in the ~3 nm subsurface region (Fig. ), and the microhardness was improved by ~45% (Fig. ). We demonstrate that nanotwins (<5 nm) could be produced in various Mn+1ACn
phases (e.g. Ti2AlC, Ti3AlC2 and Nb4AlC3) by electron irradiation and the width of The camera length was chosen to ensure that the maximum collection semi-angle was roughly three times of the convergence semi-angle (21 mrad). HAADF-STEM simulations were performed with QSTEM , where the model was set to be ~25-nm-thick based on the thickness measurement by electron energy loss spectrum. The models were sliced into 1-Å-thick layers.
The frozen phonon method was used to address the thermal diffuse scattering, where the results DFT calculation. The calculations were performed with the projector-augmented wave method using Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package .
GGA-PBE type exchange-correlation functional was used for all calculations . The equilibrium structure of Ti3AlC2 was obtained by structural optimization. The total energies and Hellmann-Feynman forces acting on atoms were converged to 10 6 eV and 0.005 eV/Å 1 , respectively. An orthogonal supercell containing 96 atoms was constructed from the hexagonal unit cell, ensuring the simulation box is larger than 10 Å along the a-, b-and c-axis to avoid image interactions.
Ed was determined by running a series of ab initio molecular dynamics simulations with different initial kinetic energies. The initial kinetic energy added to the primary knock-on atom (KPA) along [0001] was increased with a step of 1 eV until the atom moved out of their original sites.
The KPA not returned to its original position within 2 ps was regarded to be a displaced atom. Ed is the initial kinetic energy to displace KPA.
