Israel’s Elections – The Death of 2 States and the Zionist Left
Israeli politics cannot be compared with those in western capitalist democracies like Britain. The terms ‘left’ and ‘right’ are not the same in Israeli politics as elsewhere. In the West they bear some relationship to class, New Labour notwithstanding. The left has represented, in however distorted a fashion, the interests of the working class and relies on them for voting support. The right bases its appeal on private capital and appeals to the middle and bourgeois classes.
In Israel ‘left’ and ‘right’ applies to one’s position on whether to support peace with the Palestinians or a Greater Israel. Hence Ratz, the Citizen’s Rights Party, which merged into Meretz, in the 1988 Knesset, was the most liberal of Israeli parties when it came to its attitude to the Palestinians, with founder Shulamit Aloni, who became Education Minister, supporting the Refuseniks (soldiers who refuse to serve in the Occupied Territories) and adopting a non-Zionist position of opposition to the racism of a Jewish State. But economically it was a free-market position which merged with Mapam, a traditional party which originally described itself as ‘Marxist’ (in fact Stalinist).
In fact it is the Israeli working class, in particular Mizrahi/Oriental Jews, who have voted for the right in Israeli politics. Begin came to power in 1977 directly as a result of the vote of the working class. Israeli Labour was historically the enemy of the Oriental Jews and was rightly seen as their oppressor.
The Israeli Labour Party, which is erroneously seen as a party of peace, has always contained a pro-settlement wing, of which Yigal Allon and Israel Galili, of the left Ahdut Ha’avodah faction, were the most conspicuous representatives. It should never be forgot that it was Israeli Labour NOT Likud who established the first settlements and it was the Allon Plan which outlined the strategy followed to this day that the Jordan valley be colonised in order that any Palestinian state be surrounded by Jewish settlements on all sides.
The traditional parties of the Zionist Left, based on the kibbutzim and the ‘trade union’ Histadrut have been reduced to electoral insignificance. In 1949 Labour and Mapam had an absolute majority in the Knesset. Indeed David Ben Gurion, leader of Mapai, opposed building a coalition only based on the Zionist left parties and reached out to the United Religious Front and the Progressives as partners, excluding Mapam in the process.
Israeli Labour also accepted the Zionist rules of the game. No government coalition must ever depend on the votes of Arab parties. After all this is a Jewish state!
Until the 1977 elections that brought Menachem Begin of Likud to power, the Zionist left parties had never gained fewer than 54 seats and even as late as 1992, with the fateful election of Yitzhak Rabin, later to be assassinated, the Zionist left parties gained 56 seats as Meretz, which by now included Ratz, Mapam and the centre party Shinui, gained 12 seats.
But since the 1999 election the decline has been rapid. From 36 to 25 to 24 to 16 and now 13 seats, the traditional parties of the Zionist left have become irrelevant as former Chief of Staff Ehud Barak, leader of the Israeli Labour Alignment, sought to prove his macho credentials with the genocidal attack on Gaza. The explanation for the dramatic decline in Labour Zionism and the equally rapid rise of the openly racist and semi-fascist Right is two fold.
As Zeev Sternhall shows in his excellent book, The Founding Myths of Israel, the Zionist left parties were never based on class struggle. How could they since their main goal was to build a Jewish state in conjunction with Zionist and Jewish capitalists. They could hardly promise to accept such money on the basis that they were going to overthrow capitalism! Instead the Palestinians and Arab Labour were defined as the class enemy, hence the Boycott of Arab Labour campaigns of Histadrut in the 1920s and 1930s.
Colonialism in its formative and early years often takes on a co-operative form, which western social democrats mistake for socialism. Hence the Kibbutzim were on the surface egalitarian, but they operated within a colonial conquest; they were stockade and watchtower settlements. There was never a time when they were profitable and it is little wonder that as they developed industries they began to employ cheap Oriental Jewish and Arab labour. In short they became collective capitalists. And of course Kibbutzim, including those of the ‘left’ Mapam Hashomer Hatzair kibbutz federation, always excluded Arabs from membership. In other words they were thoroughly racist institutions, established on the confiscated land of the expelled Arabs.
The late Noah Lucas, a prominent but critical Zionist, described how the Kvutzah (forerunners of the Kibbutzim) were a result of
‘an alliance between the embryonic labour movement and the Zionist financial institutions. The pragmatism of the more radical socialists among the pioneers was revealed in their readiness to enter such an alliance with the Jewish bourgeoisie abroad.’
As Professor Franz Oppenheimer, who was closely involved in settling the land explained:
‘The Kvutza did not originate as a deliberate social experiment. Its forms were elaborated by accretion in the school of circumstances.’ [Noah Lucas, Modern History of Israel, p.56.]
Arthur Ruppin, the father of land settlement in Israel and a fervent believer in eugenics and the racial sciences, summed it up thus:
‘I can say with absolute certainty: those enterprises in Palestine which are most profit bearing for the businessman are almost the least profitable for the national effort and per contra many enterprises, which are least profitable for the businessman are of high national value.’ [Ruppin; Building Israel, New York 1949 pp. 47, September 1965]
Indeed the most vicious anti-Arab militia, the Palmach shock troops of the 1947-8 war, were based on the ‘Marxist’ Mapam and Ahdut Ha’avodah. It was they, under Yitzhak Rabin and Yigal Allon, who in 1948 expelled 50,000 Arabs from Lyddah and Ramleh and massacred thousands of others.
But today, when Israel is an openly capitalist society, aligning itself internationally with the most right-wing authoritarian police states, there is no room left for co-operative capitalism. Hence Histadrut’s industries were privatised in the early 1990s. Put simply, the social base of labour Zionism has all but disappeared.
The other reason that the socialist Zionist parties have declined is that their ‘peace’ proposals were based on naked racism — the need to preserve the Jewish nature of the Israeli state. In other words, there were too many Arabs. That was the basis of their support for 2 States, in reality one state, Israel, and a Palestinian Reservation. Every racist aspect of Israeli society was pioneered by Israeli labour. It was not for nothing that the settlers in the West Bank could say that their right to settle in Ariel and Kiryat Arba was the same as the original settlement of Tel Aviv. Except whereas today’s settlers base their claims on the fact that god gave them the land, the ‘left’ Zionists claimed their right to settle was based on the bible, the existence of whose god they denied!
The settler-right represent the logical culmination of Zionism and no one represents it better than the leader of Yisrael Beteinu, Avigdor Liebermann, a former member of the Jewish Nazi party Kach. YB openly questions the right of Israeli Arabs to be citizens of the Jewish State, demanding a McCarthyite ‘loyalty oath’. It wants to hive them off to a Palestinian Reservation in the West Bank. Like the revanchist nationalist myth of the ‘stab in the back’ that lost Germany the 1st world war, Liebermann openly describes Israel’s Palestinian citizens as a fifth column.
It is therefore a mark of just how far and how fast Israel has moved to the openly racist, expansionary right that Liebermann’s YB obtained 15 seats, only one less than the combined total of Israeli Labour and Meretz.
Socialists and genuine anti-racists should not be disappointed at the outcome of Israel’s elections. On the contrary, the disappearance of the hypocritical ‘shoot and cry’ brigade of ‘left’ Zionists and the ascendancy of the openly racist right is a welcome clarification of the political situation. Of course this will be blamed on Arab intransigence, but this was always the explanation of settlers — from Algeria to South Africa — of why they had to engage in yet more bloody reprisals and repression. It was Israeli Labour under Barak who led the recent attack on Gaza, just as Amir Peretz, ex-Histadrut Chairman and Defence Minister launched the attack on Lebanon in 2006.
One thing is certain. The 2 State Solution is Now Dead as a Doormouse.

?I have some good news and some bad news,? the sergeant in the joke tells his men. ?The good news is that you are going to change your dirty socks. The bad news is that you are going to exchange them among yourselves.?
I am not the only person who is reminded of this old British army joke by the current elections.
We are faced by a sorry lot of politicians, some of them documented failures and some completely free of any past achievements. There is no meaningful discussion between them about the issues. Not one of the main contenders offers real solutions to our basic problems. The differences between them are invisible without a magnifying glass.
The instinctive reaction: ?To hell with the lot of them. Let?s not vote at all!?
But that is childish. We cannot afford not to vote, or to vote out of spite or as a protest. Even if the differences are tiny ? they may turn out to be important.
Therefore, let?s hold our nose and vote. If necessary, let?s take some medicine against nausea. If all of them are bad, let?s look for the lesser evil.
FOR ME, the greatest evil is Binyamin (?Bibi?) Netanyahu.
If he gets one vote more than his rivals, the President will entrust him with the task of setting up the next government. Netanyahu has already committed himself to inviting Avigdor Liberman, the pupil of the fascist Meir Kahane, as his first partner, as well as Shas, which has now become an extreme right-wing party. Perhaps he will also take in the ?National Union?, which is even more extreme, and the remnants of the National Religious party, together with the Orthodox.
If this is to be the core of the next coalition, we shall have an extreme nationalist-racist government, a government that will reject outright any possibility of ending the occupation, setting up a Palestinian state and evacuating the settlements.
After that, Netanyahu could invite Kadima and Labor, but that would not matter anymore. Since he will be able to set up a government without them, he will get them for next to nothing. In such a government, their only function will be to serve as fig leaves, camouflage for the Americans.
One must also remember who would come with Netanyahu: types like Limor Livnat, Benny Begin and Bogie Yaalon.
Some people have brought up a Machiavellian idea: let the Likud come to power. That way, the entire world will see the true face of Israel and boycott it. The government will fall, and we can start all over again.
Sorry, that is too risky a bet for me. I am not ready to gamble with the future of Israel. To use an old catch-phrase: I don?t have another country.
Some try to cheer us up with another thought: Netanyahu is a weak person. If the Americans exert pressure on him, he will give in. In the end he will do whatever Obama tells him to do.
I am not so sure. I am not ready to bet on that either. His partners will not let him submit. For me, the first decision is: No Netanyahu.
TZIPI LIVNI has one enormous advantage: she is not Bibi.
It may seem that this is also her only advantage.
At this moment, she is the only person who could ? perhaps, perhaps ? block the road to a coalition headed by the Likud. For many, that is reason enough to vote for her.
Is there any other reason? Hard to see one. She could have risen above the murky waters and presented a clear and focused message: peace with the Palestinian people and the Arab world. That would have separated her from Netanyahu and also from Ehud Barak and given her the status of a statesperson. It would have turned the elections into a referendum on war and peace.
She has missed this opportunity. Like all the other candidates, she is afraid of the word ?peace?. Her advisors have probably warned her that the shares of peace in the stock exchange of public opinion are way down.
If she were a real leader, if peace had been burning in her bones (as we say in Hebrew), she would have ignored the advice and stood up as a woman of principle.
Instead, she is trying to be more macho than all the machos, ?The Only Man In The Government?. She cries to high heaven against any dialogue with Hamas. She objects to a mutually agreed cease-fire. She tries to compete with Netanyahu and Liberman with unbridled nationalist messages.
That is bad. That is also stupid. Someone who is looking for a he-he-man will not vote for a woman. Someone who is longing for a brutal warlord will not vote for a female civilian who, in the words of Barak, ?has never held a rifle in her hands?.
It was a test of leadership. And Tzipi flunked it.
True, here and there she has voiced some vague ideas about ?two nation-states?, but in all her years in office she has not taken the smallest real step in this direction.
Therefore, there is no reason to vote for her, except one: if she gets one vote more than Netanyahu, the President will call on her to try to set up a government. Such a government will surely include Netanyahu, and probably Liberman too. Yet it will be different from a government headed by Netanyahu. Under heavy American pressure, it might even move towards peace.
I CANNOT vote for Ehud Barak. Even if my head wanted to, my hand would not obey.
The inhuman Gaza War was a reflection of Barak?s own inhuman character. He waged the war as a part of his election campaign. When the anti-war demonstrators marched through the streets of Tel-Aviv and shouted: ?Don?t buy votes / with the blood of babies? they were not so far off the mark.
Like Netanyahu, Barak is a documented failure. I was among the masses who celebrated his triumph in Rabin Square in 1999 when he was elected Prime Minister, and, hardly a year later, I sighed with relief when his government collapsed. In his short term of office he convened the Camp David conference and sabotaged it, spread the poisonous and mendacious mantra ?We have no partner for peace?, provoked the second intifada and destroyed the peace camp from within.
Contrary to Livni, Barak does not even pretend to have a perspective of peace. He sees before him an endless landscape of mountain chains of war, mountain after mountain, stretching well beyond the horizon.
Unlike the Kadima and Likud lists, the Labor election list does include some good people. But these will have no influence at all on things to come. Effectively, it?s a one-man list, and that one man is deeply flawed.
FOR A MOMENT it seemed that Meretz was going to transform itself into something bigger. They included in their list some attractive new people. Men of letters recommended them warmly.
And then something happened to them, the same thing that happened to them the last time. A war broke out, and Meretz supported it enthusiastically. Their three literary musketeers – Amos Oz, A. B. Yehoshua and David Grossman ? went out of their way to call for the war and laud it, each one in his turn. Exactly as they had done in Lebanon War II.
True, after some days the three ? together with Meretz and Peace Now ? called for the end of the attack. That call was not accompanied by an apology for the preceding one. This showed a lot of Chutzpa. After helping in breaking the dam, they thought that they could stop the flow with their fingers. But after they had legitimized the war of atrocities, no one listened to them anymore. Every woman and child who was killed in that war, up to the very last day, should weigh on their conscience.
Of course, some will say: you don?t vote to punish and take revenge. In spite of the crime, one has to vote for Meretz because among the ?Zionist? parties they are the lesser evil. They speak about peace and social justice, and some of their representatives, like Shulamit Aloni and Yossi Sarid, did a good job in the Rabin government. Meretz also did some good parliamentary work for the right causes.
QUITE ANOTHER problem is posed by the three so-called ?Arab? parties, one of which is the communist Hadash, which has a small Jewish component.
The Hadash program is closer to the consistent peace camp than any other. Some would say: That?s close enough. I vote according to my beliefs, and not tactical considerations. Hadash should also be credited for advancing some positive causes in the Knesset.
The problem of the ?Arab? lists is that they have not succeeded in playing a meaningful role in the political arena, which has remained an exclusive fiefdom of the ?Zionist? parties (?Zionist? in this context means ?non Arab?). In order to break into the Jewish street, Hadash could have put at the head of its list, or at least in the No. 2 slot, Dov Khenin, who has risen to stardom in the recent Tel-Aviv municipal elections. By not doing so, they have lost at least some of the votes that could have strayed from Meretz and Labor.
The impact of the ?Arab? parties on Israeli policy is next to nil. It is limited to one point in time: on the day after the elections, the question will arise whether all the center/left parties together, from Kadima leftwards, can muster enough votes to block a right-wing government. In this context, and only there, the ?Arab? parties do play a role.
THERE REMAINS the Liberman phenomenon.
Liberman has created a party that is simply and thoroughly racist. Its election campaign is centered on the demand to annul the Israeli citizenship of ?non-loyal? people. Meaning: the Arabs, who constitute 20% of Israel?s citizens.
In every other country, Liberman?s program would be called fascist, without quotation marks. Nowhere in the Western world is there a large party that would dare to advance such a demand. The neo-fascists in Switzerland and Holland want to expel foreigners, not to annul the citizenship of the native-born.
The core of the party is made up of immigrants from the former Soviet Union, many of whom have brought from their homeland an utter contempt for democracy, a desire for a strong leader (a Stalin or a Putin), a racist attitude towards brown-skinned citizens and a taste for brutal, Chechnya-style wars. They have now been joined by young, native-born Israelis, who have been radicalized by the recent war.
When Joerg Haider was taken into the Austrian cabinet, Israel recalled its ambassador from Vienna in protest. But compared to Liberman, Haider was a raving liberal, and so is Jean-Marie le Pen. Now Netanyahu has announced that Liberman will be ?an important minister? in his government, Livni has hinted that he will be in her government, too, and Barak has not excluded that possibility.
The optimistic version says that Liberman will prove to be a passing curiosity. Every Israeli election campaign has featured a trend-party that reflects a passing mood, achieves a resounding success and then disappears. In 1977 it was the Dash party, which rode the horse of ?changing the system?. It won 12.5% of the vote, broke apart and disappeared before the next elections. Later it was the Tzomet party of Rafael Eitan, on the horse of uncorrupted purity. Another was the Shinui (Change) party, which rode the horse of anti-religious hatred and disappeared without leaving a trace. In the last elections it was the pensioners? list, with tens of thousands of youngsters voting for it as a prank. In the current elections, Liberman?s party has caught the trend, riding on the primitive emotions of the masses which broke free in the Gaza War.
There is also a pessimistic version: Fascism has become a serious player in the Israeli public domain. The three main parties have now legitimized it. This phenomenon must be stopped before it is too late.
SO, HOW shall I vote this coming Tuesday?
I intend to draw up a list that will start from the worst down to the least evil. The last one on the list gets my vote.

TITLE : Navigating Sustainability: A Case Study of the Bristol Food System in Proposing Solutions to Challenges for Sustainable Food Organizations
INTRODUCTION:
The multifaceted role of this proposal of a sustainable food organization is highlighted in this all-encompassing overview. It focuses on the interaction of key elements such as activities, flows, stakeholders, technologies, and sustainability in the design of an innovative and sustainable agri-food value chain model (Corallo et al., 2023). The proposal underlines the requisite strategic approach to tackle environmental concerns and climate change-related challenges through sustainability’s promotion as an integral feature for societal progress. The proposal suggests the need for a framework law on sustainable food systems to foster human and planetary health and direct innovation towards more sustainable farming, food processing, and consumption (Poppe, 2023).
Bristol’s method of food system organization is an exceptional example of sustainability with its innovative and comprehensive approach. The city of Bristol is currently exploring the obstacles faced by its food system as it strives to develop a robust and adaptable plan. The food system in Bristol faces various societal challenges, including food waste, nutrient overload in water systems, food security issues, energy and carbon footprint, plastic contamination, sewage system blockages, and difficulties in recycling sewage and wastewater (Carey, 2013). To address these challenges, the city is focusing on reducing residential food waste and processing, as well as improving resilience and economic efficiency in the food-energy-water nexus (Wood et al., 2023). The goal is to transform Bristol into a sustainable food city by involving citizens and decision-makers and implementing effective mechanisms for planning and change (Ruben et al., 2021).
To achieve long-term resilience in the face of these challenges , Bristol recognizes the interconnectedness of its food system while also identifying strengths and vulnerabilities (Carey, 2013). Urban agriculture has a vital role to play in increasing this resilience , building community bonds via diverse local supply networks that promote healthier eating habits while supporting social justice initiatives at every level (Mark, 2014). The city council can contribute to resilience and social justice by implementing interventions such as procurement policies, urban planning, and supporting urban agriculture initiatives (Reed and Keech, 2017). The development of urban food policies is a shared responsibility between the city council, private sector, and voluntary sector actors. The food policy in Bristol is seen as a social movement, with activism aimed at sustainability and inclusivity (Black et al., 2023)
Taking together, these studies outline how critical Bristol has become as a contemporary illustration of sustainable organizational practices when it comes to resource management.
PROBLEM :
Bristol’s food system stakeholders are working towards a sustainable, resilient and inclusive food plan (Carey, 2013). This objective is being achieved through grassroots networks and social movements that aim to impact policy-making processes at the municipal level (Reed, 2019). The city’s urban food policies are perceived as contested arenas where more equitable narratives around nutrition can be cultivated (Moragues-Faus, 2015), whilst emphasis is also placed on promoting participatory measures with broad socio-economic appeal in order to secure just culinary futures for all citizens under state patronage.
Available secondary data shows that the analysis of Bristol’s food system covers a period from 2016 to 2021. This timeframe coincides with the initiation of the Bristol Going for Gold project aimed at promoting involvement in Good Food Movement through six themes, which include purchasing superior quality food products; consuming healthy meal options; minimizing waste production related to edible items and backing communal endeavors regarding urban cultivation and equitable access to dietary essentials.
Carey (2013) highlights the importance of a comprehensive approach involving citizens and city decision makers in achieving a sustainable food system in Bristol. Reed (2019) suggests that urban groups and business associations can play an influential role through bottom-up, horizontal networks to shape policy and municipal strategies. To further enhance sustainability efforts, addressing convenience and cost barriers by co-designing waste reduction services for catering purposes as proposed by Michalec (2018), could be effective. In addition, Stierand’s (2016) observation on establishing Food Policy Councils similar to Brighton & Hove is crucial towards shaping successful urban food systems.
To tackle the challenges within Bristol’s food system, several key areas must be addressed. Effective stakeholder engagement and collaboration are crucial (Carey, 2013), alongside a focus on post-farm gate activities such as processing, packaging and distribution to ensure adequate food security (Ingram, 2013). Additionally, successful sustainable food provision requires bottom-up grassroots networks rather than top-down approaches (Reed 2019). The catering sector faces notable obstacles with regards to recycling waste products including convenience cost or space restrictions (Michalec , 2018).
The Bristol food system Is utilizing diverse approaches to address concerns pertaining to food, such as procuring high-quality products, reducing waste production and promoting urban farming while ensuring fair distribution of nutrition. Implementation of these methods has yielded notable results – for instance; household recycling saw a surge by 38% between the period of 2016-2020 with Olio app witnessing an increase in shared meals by over 12.1k% within Bristol since its inception four years ago!
While certain aspects of these methods have yielded success, there are notable restrictions that must be addressed. The Olio app’s contribution to food sharing is unquestionable; yet, some demographics may face challenges in accessing the platform. Furthermore, while preventable waste has reduced and recycling efforts for edible items increased, eliminating wastage altogether calls for more household and commercial-level actions. Notably, COVID-19 had a significant impact on local restaurants’ business models as well as farm-to-fork businesses requiring continued innovation and support strategies moving forward.
Collaboration among citizens, decision makers and diverse stakeholders is crucial in effectively addressing significant components of the Bristol food system. Carey (2013) emphasizes that effective mechanisms are required to bring together the right participants while Ingram (2013) stresses on incorporating various perspectives like policy, private sector and advocacy groups for dealing with food security elements. The importance of civil society, private actors and local governments in creating sustainable urban foodscapes as well influencing municipal policies is highlighted by Moragues-Faus (2015) and Reed( 2019).
In conclusion, Bristol has made significant progress in addressing food waste and promoting sustainable eating practices within its food system. However, there are still limitations and ongoing challenges that require sustained efforts and innovative approaches to establish a truly enduring and eco-friendly culinary industry in the city.

VISION INTO PRACTICE
The purpose of this report is to critically analyze Bristol's implementation of a sustainable food system using customer journey mapping. As a case study of Bristol's food initiative, we examine how social issues and sustainable business practices are interconnected. In order to ensure a rigorous evaluation framework for Bristol's approach to a resilient food system, journey mapping will be used to illuminate key academic literature. This analysis demonstrates how strategic visions can be linked to sustainable outcomes.
Bristol Food Context and Vision
There are global sustainability issues such as food security and environmental impact reflected in Bristol's food system. Bristol's “Going for Gold” initiative seeks to transform food production, community engagement, and health (Bristol Going for Gold, n.d.). In addition to supporting global sustainable development discourse, this initiative stresses the interdependence of ecological, social, and economic systems (Agyeman & DeVries, 2021). Bristol’s vision is therefore a manifestation of broader sustainability narratives that aim to change food practices systemically, aligning with the New Environmental Economics (Jenkins, 2019).
A multi-stakeholder approach is necessary to address the complex urban food systems (Wood et al., 2023) by bringing together government, businesses, and civil society groups. Bristol Good Food 2030 envisions increasing local food production, reducing waste, and improving public health. To this effect, Howard-Grenville (2021) emphasizes policy innovation and community engagement as these goals converge (Howard-Grenville, 2021).
Based on evidence, key reports (Carey, 2013) and initiatives (Bristol Going for Gold, n.d.) outline an ambitious roadmap. This report details Bristol's resilient food system's progress and challenges, providing critical insights into the potential for replicating such models in other urban contexts.
Journey Mapping Process
In this analysis, Bristol's food system's sustainability progress is detailed through the journey mapping process. Clarke & Crane (2018) and Grey et al., (2015) acknowledge that there is a  variety of behaviors, mindsets, and emotions encountered during this process of complexity-sensitive cross-sector partnerships. Data were analysed from reports, alongside policy documents, and stakeholder interviews using collaborative practices (Waddell, 2011).
At each stage, the narrative was linked to module concepts such as resilience and social impact (Benn, Dunphy, & Griffiths, 2014) to provide a holistic understanding of the initiatives. The goals, challenges, and resulting emotional landscape of Bristol's food system were analysed by tracing the touch-points of actor interactions (Könnölä et al., 2017).
A critical literature review on transformational business models (Nicholls & Murdock, 2012) and societal sustainability (Schaltegger & Wagner, 2017) guided the thematic analysis, allowing us to consider what actions were taken,  and why.

Title: “Ripple in Abstraction”

Synopsis:

In an infinite realm of swirling shapes and vibrant colors – a universe unfettered by the laws of nature or logic – lives Ripple, a young rabbit with insatiable curiosity and boundless energy. Faced with an existence amidst chaos, where concepts such as ground, sky, or even time don’t adhere to any known rules, Ripple seeks to find some semblance of meaning and connection in an otherwise completely abstract world.

Act I:

Ripple’s adventure begins with an innocent question, “What lies beyond the abstract?” Unlike his surroundings, Ripple possesses form, consciousness, and a thirst for understanding, traits that set him apart in this limitless expanse of abstraction. The world around him is a kaleidoscope of feelings, colors, and movement – beautiful but bewildering.

Ripple encounters a variety of abstract entities – shapes that shift between dimensions, colors that evoke emotions Ripple can barely comprehend, and sounds that seem to tell stories without words. Despite the beauty and joy these elements bring, Ripple feels an underlying sense of loneliness, realizing that he is the only being of his kind.

Act II:

Determined to find others like him or at least understand his place in this reality, Ripple embarks on a journey that takes him through surreal landscapes, each more inexplicable than the last. Through a series of challenges, Ripple discovers he has the unique ability to influence the abstract world around him by projecting his thoughts and emotions, creating ripples that reorder the chaos into something momentarily comprehensible.

During his voyage, Ripple befriends a series of peculiar characters: a shape-shifting cloud that can mimic any form but struggles with its own identity, a radiant orb that communicates through music and can illuminate the darkest corners of abstraction, and a fractal creature that can foresee the infinite paths Ripple’s journey might take. Together, they navigate the abstract domain, seeking a place where Ripple might belong.

Act III:

The closer Ripple and his companions get to the heart of the abstract world, the more they realize that the quest for understanding might be endless. They encounter The Absence, a void that threatens to unmake everything Ripple has learned and experienced. In facing The Absence, Ripple understands that the essence of his journey is not about finding a conventional home or others of his kind but about creating meaning and connection in an environment that defies both.

In the climax, Ripple confronts The Absence with the power of his newfound insights, his emotions, and his companions by his side. Together, they transform The Absence, not by filling it with form or logic, but by accepting it as part of the balance between the concrete and the abstract. Ripple learns that his existence is not an anomaly but a bridge between worlds, a spark of consciousness that brings depth to the beauty of abstraction.

Epilogue:

Ripple decides to continue exploring the vast abstract realm, no longer searching for something to fill a void but eager to expand the connections he’s made. Alongside his friends, Ripple becomes a guardian of the balance, a guide for others who might one day find themselves lost in the abstraction, teaching them to find peace in the beauty of the undefined and the power of their own perception to shape reality.

“Ripple in Abstraction” ends with a panoramic view of the abstract world, now slightly less chaotic, more vibrant with the ripples of understanding that spread far and wide, suggesting that every search for meaning, no matter how seemingly small or different, enriches the fabric of the universe.  On December 3, 1984 Dragon Ball's Sun Goku was introduced to the public, and over the last 35 years has become one of the most recognizable and prolific characters of the modern age. From TV shows to commercials to blockbuster movies, from video games to parades to being the mascot for the 2020 Olympic Games, you would assume for one to accrue such incredible success, said character would need to be widely accepted as a good one, or at least a well-written one. However, nowadays there's a strongly held belief that if a character doesn't develop or grow from an experience, then that character in question is a poorly written one. Therefore to test this theory, a while back I posted a poll on my Twitter asking the question, if given the choice between Goku and Vegeta, who'd you prefer, and why? The one that was close with over 4,000 votes cast Vegeta 1. With the majority of people who voted for Vegeta bolstering their choice by arguing, Vegeta has grown and changed a considerable amount over his character arc. Goku has no arc. He remains the same. While most of the statement is technically correct, this led me to believe that on a fundamental narrative level, the character of Sun Goku is deeply misunderstood by an enormous portion of the viewership because Goku does have a character arc. He is a terrific example of what writers call the Flat Character arc. In 2016, KM Wild and Publisha Book called, Create and Character arcs, in which she describes three character arc methods. The Positive Character arc? This is the most common character arc found in fiction where the character undergoes a positive change. The Negative Character arc, where the character undergoes a negative change, and finally, the Flat Character arc, which we will be discussing in this video. In order to make sense of the Flat Character arc, it's important to understand the most common arc in storytelling first. The Positive Character arc, in which the character and question spends their entire journey overcoming a specific lie they hold to be true, Wild and calls this script writing trope. The lie the character believes. A wonderful example of this positive character arc is observed with the character of Vegeta. For his entire existence, Vegeta has been someone who believed that power was the only important thing in life. And to pursue anything else would be a fool's errand. This was the lie Vegeta believed. And throughout his life, this lie was reinforced by the world around him. Through pursuing this end, Vegeta sacrificed his everything to achieve his goal. It's his belief in this lie that leads him to die on planet Namik. When faced with the reality his choices have led him to, he crumbles, and ultimately falls. Vegeta's lie was that he believed the only value to be found in life was through the pursuit of power. And his arc was about the journey he took in order to overcome this lie and to embrace what was actually true. To find value in those he loved. And in that moment the viewer and Vegeta share a much-needed catharsis. As while in writes, the Positive Character arc is about the lie the character believes, which he will spend the entire journey overcoming. However, unlike the Positive Character arc which tells the story based on a lie the character believes, the flat character arc is about the truth the character believes. In the flat character arc the protagonist already has a handle on what the truth is. And he will use that truth to overcome the challenges of the plot. And probably to transform a lie-burdened world. One of the defining features of the flat arc is that the character begins his journey to already believing in a certain truth. So in Goku is an enthusiastic, innocent and motivated person who believes that he can always be better today than he is tomorrow. And not in a diminishing or deprecating way he thrives annoying he can be better tomorrow than he is today. And these ideals have not changed since he was first introduced to us in the mid-80s. To help prove that I'm not making these points up, here are some other characters that fit this mold too. Forced Gun is an honest, compassionate and determined individual who wants to find and be with the person he loves, Jenny, and from the beginning of the film to the end his outlook on life never falters reflected in the famous quote, Life is like a box of chocolates. You never know what you're going to get until you take that first bite. Indiana Jones is a determined and courageous man who believes in doing what is right. From the outset these are what his ideals are and what makes his story compelling isn't how he changes but how the world around him reacts to these characteristics he possesses. The titan is an infinitely powerful otherwise ordinary guy with strong morals and ideals for what he thinks a hero should be, bored by conventional crime fighting he earns for the thrill of a real challenge. And despite never actually getting that, his personality and ideals don't waver. He is human but he is also a real hero. What I find personally interesting about all of these characters is, none of them are really praised or remembered for being great characters. Instead people will often say, for a scum is an amazing movie, or that one punchman was a great TV series. However a fundamental difference between for a scum but one punchman is that one is a movie and the other is a television show. Rarely will you see someone say that the character for a scum is a bad one but people will flat out dismiss one punchman on its main character as very premise alone. Personally I think the length of a TV series versus a movie plays a large factor here. People expect a desire a TV shows characters to grow and develop over the series in order to justify its long length. Specific emphasis is put on shows like Dragon Ball, Naruto or One Piece because their theme is sent around self-improvement. Whereas in a film it's not as noticeable if their characters don't develop over the course of its runtime. If we look closely at the character of Sun Goku, we observe from the very beginning of the show, his character is fundamentally at odds with the story and world around. This is a writing technique specifically used for characters that utilize a flat arc and so while Goku himself believes the truth from the outset, pretty much all those he interacts with believes a lot and the intrigue for the journey comes from Goku's sensibilities changing the world around him for the better. For example, this is a very important thing. Or if you want an even earlier example, here's this. Despite Master Oshih having taken a considerable amount of his life to perfect the Kamehameha, Goku managed to learn it with relative ease. However the most noticeable example of Goku changing the world around him using the truth he has is right here. On top of changing the world around him, he also changes the supporting cast for the better too. The characters like Master Oshih are now retired because Goku is now the new savior of the earth. Characters like Ten Shinhan, Piccolo and Vegeta have changed from bad to good because of his actions. The reason why Goku remains the focus of Dragon Ball is due to one simple fact. Goku is Dragon Ball. Everything that happens in Dragon Ball is due to this character and it can't be any other way. So let me explain why. Goku's character is ideal for a long running show because unlike Vegeta and Piccolo, his arc doesn't have an expiry date. Vegeta's character was praised in its climax, but because the show wanted to continue, his development had to be altered and slightly red-cut at the beginning of Dragon Ball super. During which they had to repeat certain key scenes to invoke a similar reaction from the fanbase. The same we said for Piccolo, jumping in front of Gohan blocking a blast during the resurrection F arc, it's just not the same because as the show reflects, his time in the sun is over. On a much more real level, Gohan's story is absolutely over. It ended itself. That was the coming of age moment and nothing he can do will ever top that. Unless they drastically revamped, reinvent or retcon his character. But unlike Vegeta, Piccolo and Gohan, Goku is not restricted by such conventions due to the nature of his story arc. Because Goku doesn't need to change or grow from an experience, the intrigue when he interacts with a character or situation comes from how the world or that character reacts to Goku. So technically, Goku and characters like Goku that implement the flat arc have as much intrigue as the world around them does. And as I'm sure many writers would tell you, it's much easier to create interesting tasks and worlds for Goku to explore than it would be for someone to write another way for Vegeta to swallow his pride and for us to care about it. The point that I'm trying to make here is, despite his unwavering sensibilities, Goku has remained engaging throughout. Specifically when he is written by a curatorial Yamaha, who understood that the character of Goku needed to have a flat arc if he wanted to have the flexibility to write a week to week manga chapter. Goku is a flexible engaging character because he utilizes the flat character arc. And that is why this particular arc has value. And so with the stigma nowadays claiming that Goku is a boring character because he has no personal development, I feel compelled to say, no, that's not a fair assessment at all. On top of the positive character arc being the most common arc in character writing, and one of the most noticeable, it also seems to be the only one given any spotlight at all. Rarely does someone talk about a negative character arc which would be observed with characters like Yagami from Death Note or even Zamasu from Dragon Ball Super. This is when a character goes from a good or benign standing to that of a villain or changes for the worse. Even a flat arc like Goku's can be subdivided into categories, Goku is a positive flat arc. And an example of a negative flat arc can be observed with characters like Freeze, who are evil to the core, unwavering, manipulating the world around them instead of the world changing them. One of the reason why Freeze and Goku's interactions are so compelling, because they are both steadfast in their beliefs. I am certainly not trying to claim that one character arc is superior to the other, but merely pointing out certain advantages the flat arc might have over the others because of its design. So just to reiterate, Dragon Ball cannot be Dragon Ball without Goku. And while wonderful characters like Piccolo and Vegeta are thrilling and fun to watch, I think it's important to acknowledge that Goku's character has value 2, but in a vastly different way.

Which to me is a shame because if Goku attained ultra instinct for a genuine growth and development reason rather than just simply getting it, it would have given an already very cool scene and emotional weight behind it that we don't normally see with Goku in the circumstances. It would have made it a very unique moment for Goku specifically in the series. And that's just it in a nutshell. Instead of arcs flowing into each other as consistently and cohesively as the original series did, many arcs have beginning points and end points. Things suddenly happen because plot needs to happen and characters are given things to work on that really if you think about it long enough, don't make a lot of sense for the character. In the entire series, the closest instance I could find to Adolf Goku actually having misplaced confidence in himself was early in the freezer fight. He never believed the fight would be easy, but he wasn't prepared for how monstrous freezer really was. However, to paint this as overconfidence, I think is a stretch. And even if you consider it full blown over confidence, to consider this one instance grounds to label Goku as a definitive overconfident character is I think disingenuous. But at the end of the day, writing is still one of the most difficult things when it comes to art. Dragon Ball Super captured my imagination and for that alone I would label it as success. But just because I like and enjoy something doesn't mean that I have to turn a blind eye instead of questioning things. For me that's one of the more fun aspects of watching a TV show. Hearing out how it's written and where it doesn't make sense, and that really was the impetus for this entire anatomy of anime series. I'm so incredibly thankful that so many of you have decided to share your mornings after known that evenings with me over this last year. I'm truly humbled and will continue to try my best to improve. But until then, let me know what you think about Wiesus comments towards Goku down below. Do you think he's overconfident? Am I right? Am I wrong? Let me know. But that'll do it for this week. I've been totally not Mark. Thank you so much for watching.

"Smile, my dear! You know, you're never fully dressed without one!"―Alastor, after seeing Vaggie frown
Alastor, also known as The Radio Demon, is a sinner demon and is one of the many powerful Overlords of Hell. He is one of the main protagonists of Hazbin Hotel.
He has offered to assist Charlie Morningstar in her endeavors, albeit, for his own amusement.

Appearance
Alastor is a slim, dapper sinner demon, with beige colored skin, and usually having a broad smile full of sharp, yellow teeth. He is approximately the same height as his rival, Vox, with the two of them standing at approximately 7 feet.
He sports a pinkish-red cropped, angled bob-cut with black tips at the ends and two large, black tipped tufts of hair extending from the top of his head, evoking the ears of a deer. The style has an undercut at the back, and two small black antlers protuding from the crown, which can grow in size in his full demonic form.
His eyes have dark-red sclerae, bright-red irises and thin black pupils (which can change into the shape of radio dials when shifting into his full demon form). He also wears a dark-red oval-shaped monocle, rimmed with black, over his right eye.
Alastor wears a red pinstripe coat with dark-red lapels piped with white, which is ragged along the bottom hem. Underneath this he wears a bright red dress-shirt with a black cross on the chest, and long black dress pants with matching bright red cuffs.
He accessorizes with a black knotted bowtie with a bright red center, black gloves with red at the fingertips, and black pointed-toe boots with red deer hoofprints emblazoned on the soles. Alastor also carries a thin cane with a sentient vintage style microphone attached to it, which he uses to play sound effects and broadcast his voice.

Personality
Alastor stands out from many of the more chaotic residents of hell for his well maintained amiable persona. He gives the first-impression of a good-natured and charming man, wearing a permanently wide grin on his face at all times.
Alastor's behavior, mannerisms, and even his voice are similar to an old-fashioned radio announcer and speaks with a transatlantic accent, often using quaint anachronisms such as "the picture show" and refers to Charlie as a "charming demon belle".
This playful dandyish exterior, however, obscures a much darker side to him - one with high levels of self-importance - and he will not hesitate to use physical violence when others don't act in line with his very particular values or expectations.
Alastor is described as a man of duality. He values good manners, affability and intelligence very highly in others, and will actively look down on those who do not meet his standards, however he will often play fast and loose with these arbitrary rules in regards to himself and his own conduct. His smiling is also a show of power and dominance, and miserable people are seen by him as weak.
Alastor has an odd sense of morality, which is described as "not normal", and has been noted to be quite sadistic, even cannibalistic, devouring lesser demons or those that have incurred his anger. Despite this, he keeps close friends with the other cannibals of Hell, including the denizens at the Cannibal Colony.
He is noted to be narcissistic, not seeing many people quite up to his level. However, that does not make him reckless. Despite being extremely powerful, Alastor is aware that there are other demons and entities that rival him in terms of power, such as other Overlords. For this reason, he is wary around such demons, as they could potentially harm him if he is not careful.
Despite everything, Alastor does genuinely seem to want to help Charlie run the Happy Hotel, albeit for his own amusement and hopes for its failure over siding with her idealism. Alastor also dismisses the idea that redemption is possible as laughable, nevertheless, he fulfills his role as patron as promised, providing the hotel with staff, and protecting Charlie and her business from outside threats. He views the whole endeavor as a fun distraction from his decades of boredom.

Abilities
Natural Abilities
Demon Transformation - In flashbacks featured in the pilot, as well as in the official Alastor-centric comic, Alastor has demonstrated the ability to turn into a more powerful Demon form.
Flexibility - Alastor can contort his body into numerous unnatural poses.

Skillset
Deal-making - Alstor is shown to be a deal-maker demon in the pilot, offering Charlie a deal in return for his help with the hotel, something she wisely turns down. Deal-maker demons like Alastor can increase their power by dealing in souls, which is a very powerful commodity in hell. So they’re seen as very manipulative and not to be toyed with. Deal-making is not something every demon can do, as such it is not to be taken lightly as it doesn’t generally work out well for the other party.
Broadcasting - While living, Alastor's profession was as a radio show host, and he continues his broadcasts in Hell, ensuring that Hell's denizens are aware of his activities over the airwaves, earning him the title of "The Radio Demon".
Bilingualism - Alastor can speak English fluently as well as some broken Creole French.
Cooking - Alastor is noted to be "a big foodie" and mentions having admired his mother's cooking in the pilot, specifically her Jambalaya.
Musical, Dancing, and Theatrical Talent - Alastor is shown to display moderate vocal abilities and excels at dancing, with tap being a style he excels in specifically. He also shows a flair for theatrical showmanship.
Wide Intellect- Alastor is shown to be quite a cunning individual, resulting in him accruing a large amount of power through his tricks and deal-making.

Unique Abilities
Demonic Magic - Alastor can cast magic thanks to the high power-level he has accrued in the demon ranking system. In the pilot, this takes the visual form of glowing red symbols that resemble Voodoo veve, which float around him. Alastor is also shown using a type of blood magic, clenching his fist until droplets of blood can be seen falling from it, as a means to defeat Sir Pentious.
Shadow Manipulation - Alastor is able to summon shadows and manipulate them into doing his bidding.
Spatial Warping - Alastor is able to get around with the help of his shadow. This was first shown when he teleports behind Charlie and Vaggie after entering the hotel for the first time.
Portal Creation - Alastor can also transport others to his location easily via the portals he makes. This is shown when he pulls Niffty out of a fireplace he summons, as well as pulling Husk (along with a portion of the bar he was in) into the hotel foyer.
Pyrokinesis - Alastor summons a ball of fire to distract Charlie as he shoves Vaggie away before starting his reprise.
Phytokinesis - As shown in the comics, Alastor is able to make plants wilt with a single stare.
Manifestation - Alastor manifests a bottle of cheap alcohol to bribe Husk back into his service.
Photokinesis - During his introduction, he is shown to be able to project red glowing light from his eyes as well as his microphone.
Outfit Alteration - Alastor is capable of changing the outfits of his targets as well as his own with a snap of a finger.

Trivia
Alastor's name can be translated from ancient Greek to "spirit of revenge" or "tormentor".
Alastor was stated to be from New Orleans, Louisiana when he was alive.
He was an only child.
His ethnicity was mixed-race Creole.
He was a radio show host and prolific serial killer. He's described as "living that good life/his best life" while a radio star.
"Not going after just anyone", highlighting his "weird moral code". He share some similarities with the fictional serial killer, Dexter.
Alastor wasn't a cannibal while he was alive.
Alastor speaks with a Transatlantic (sometimes called a Mid-Atlantic) accent. A fashionable affect for American newscasters in the 1920s' to adopt, it was a combination of an idealized American accent and the clipped upper-class Queen's English used by the British Broadcasting Corporation in their "World Service" radio news.
Alastor can speak some French, although not fluently.
The pilot makes several references to Alastor's love for his mother. He is "a momma's boy".
Alastor was a big theater person while living and would see everything. His general media preferences would be the "elevated horror" genre, as well as smart, dry comedies, such as the work of Buster Keaton.
He's mot afraid of dogs, but he actively dislikes them due to "backstory reasons" which involve his death, an event he apparently did not appreciate.
Alastor had been shot in the head by a hunter while attempting to bury a body on a hunting ground. The red 'X' on Alastor's forehead, seen glowing in the pilot when he uses his demon powers, may be a visual reference to this.
Although Alastor is not a hard drinker, he does favor the hard liquors when he chooses to drink, such as whiskey. His New Orleans background is cited for his "party side", emphasizing that he is a "classy drunk, not a messy drunk".
Alastor likes black coffee, but does not like tea.
Alastor is a big foodie and enjoys cooking. He is also something of a food snob, and hates "lazy" processed foods. Alastor probably isn't much of a fan of sweet things either, preferring bitter tastes, like meat and whiskey.
Alastor enjoys meat raw.
Alastor enjoys visiting Cannibal Colony and frequents the cafes there, relating a lot to the residents and enjoying the food.
Alastor's powers are "lots of things". Alastor is a character that keeps many abilities hidden as he enjoys being unpredictable. He will sometimes feign an inability to do things that he can actually do, partly to subvert expectations, partly to be intentionally antagonistic and force the people around him to struggle with something he could easily have done.
Alastor can take on many forms.
Whenever Alastor uses his powers in the pilot, he is shown emitting a faint red aura.
He can be seen using a form of Voodoo inspired blood magic as a means to defeat Sir Pentious in the pilot.
Alastor's microphone is a living extension of himself that he can manifest and hide whenever he chooses. He hypothetically would not be able to talk without it, but that it's not something that can ever be separated from him, as it's not a tangible object to anyone but Alastor.
Alastor's planned room at the hotel is a mixture between both traditional decor and the fantastical, with one half being a classic "fancy study", complete with tasteful wallpaper and furnishings, the other half being a literal swamp conjured as a dining area. He is the type of person to own two homes, one a fancy townhouse, the other a rickety hunting lodge in a bayou on stilts.
Alastor simultaneously does and does not care about neatness. He doesn't mind being covered in blood and viscera, and will calmly clean up after himself, but he is bothered by other things, such as people being messy eaters around him. There's a comparison to a Hannibal Lecter-like figure, who is very sophisticated about things.
Alastor's favorite song has been stated to be the one that partially inspired him: "You're Never Fully Dressed Without a Smile" from the musical, Annie. As for songs specific to Alastor's time period, it would be "Smile" by Charlie Chaplin. Cab Calloway was also mentioned as a favorite singer, with an emphasis on Alastor's love of jazz in both life and death.
Alastor can play several instruments, including the piano, violin, trumpet, and saxophone. It is part of Alastor's canon that he both owns, and can play, a 'Furby organ'.
Alastor enjoys occasionally impromptu joining in with bands that are playing. He loves to cook and prepare dishes, although in his own way as he prefers his meat raw. He also enjoys playing pranks on others.
Alastor loves the fact that he scares people.
Alastor is not a fan of modern technology and doesn't like using any technology that was invented after he died. This plays a part in his not getting along with Vox, who has fully embraced it.
Alastor is said to not be a big fan of children and although he wouldn't kill a child, he would strike one if they annoyed him too much, believing in "that kind of discipline". He also won't take responsibility if the child accidentally injures itself when he lets them play.
Alastor would be a bad father, although a better mentor figure.
Alastor's jovial remark on there being "so many orphans" during the stock market crash of 1929 in the pilot, implies he is apathetic to children's suffering.
Alastor is capable of forming friendships and can become fond of people, although in his own particular way. He becomes fond of people he sees as especially funny or entertaining.
Alastor interacts on better terms with women in general, and is much lighter in his view of them. He doesn't view many of the other powerful male characters within his circle as providing any substantially intelligent conversation, seeing them as "stupid idiot brutes" and not thinking very highly of them for the most part. Others, such as Angel and Husk, he finds pitiable.
Alastor greatly values manners in others and is personally offended by disrespect and rudeness. He also values humor, enjoying when people can give him a good view of their misery.
Alastor is one of the few Sinners who has not taken on a new name in Hell. Instead, he keeps with his true name from his living life, as he is not a fan of making nicknames for himself.He is, however, happy to be referred to as "Al".
He can also dematerialize to avoid things.
Alastor does not respect the personal space of others at all, grabbing and pulling around Charlie, Vaggie, and Husk numerous times in the pilot.
Alastor wears gloves. They are charcoal grey with red tips at the nails.
Alastor apparently is not particularly big on oral hygiene, with VivziePop describing his breath as "not good", and in fact he has black gums.
The red treads on the soles of Alastor's shoes resemble deer hoof tracks, he has antlers, and two tufts of his hair that evoke the ears of a deer.]

Lilith's description: [NICKNAMES: Mom (by Charlie), Queen of Hell
SPECIES: Demon

PROFESSIONAL STATUS: Queen of Hell

OCCUPATION: Co-ruler of the Pride Ring, Performer

Lilith is the queen of Hell, the wife of Lucifer Morningstar, and the mother of Charlie Morningstar. She is a character in Hazbin Hotel.

Appearance
Lilith is presented as a tall, slender, curvaceous woman, exceeding both her husband and daughter in height.
Estimates point her to be approximately 6 feet and 4-6 inches (193-198 centimeters) tall.
She has pale skin, thin eyebrows and silver-grey eyes, long black eyelashes and extremely long, light blonde hair with thick honey blonde streaks reaching down to the floor.
Unlike her husband, she has a pair of long, magenta horns which noticeably differs depending on the scenario. This is because she is able to change the shape of her horns at will.

Personality
Lilith's is graceful, regal, and politically charged.
Lilith is someone who is exceptionally equanimous.
She is somewhat good with children.

Trivia
The name "Lilith" translates to "night-bird", "screech owl", "night hag" or "night-spectre" from Hebrew text.
Lilith is a former cabaret dancer. Like her family, Lilith loves music, as evidenced by her career as a singer in Hell, as well as the fact that Vivziepop's headcanon voice for her is Lady Gaga.
Lilith and Lucifer's dynamic can be summed up with the phrase, "Behind every man is a greater woman", and that they love each other very much. Lilith and Lucifer are described as "passionate, cheesy lovers".
Lilith "wears the pants" in her family, but in fact both Lilith and Lucifer are switches within their intimate life.
Lilith and Charlie, alongside Alastor, are fans of pineapple on pizza.]

Cooperative Resource Scheduling for Time-Sensitive Services
in an Integrated XGS-PON and Wi-Fi 6 Network
Jun Li ,S a n j a yK .B o s e ,Senior Member, IEEE , and Gangxiang Shen ,Senior Member, IEEE
Abstract — 10-Gbps symmetrical passive optical network
(XGS-PON) and Wi-Fi 6 are two key technologies to providegigabit access for the ﬁfth-generation ﬁxed network (F5G).However, how to integrate XGS-PON and Wi-Fi 6 to meet F5G’sstringent quality of service requirements is still a challenge.In this letter, we propose a cooperative resource schedulingscheme, in which a communication tunnel is established toachieve a low end-to-end (E2E) delay by sharing medium accesscontrol information between XGS-PON and Wi-Fi 6. Simulationresults show that the proposed scheme can signiﬁcantly reducethe E2E delay for time-sentinel services by up to 50% withoutsacriﬁcing the performance of non-time-sensitive services.
Index Terms — Cooperative resource scheduling, passive optical
network, Wi-Fi 6, time-sensitive service.
I. I NTRODUCTION
THE ﬁfth-generation ﬁxed network (F5G) is envisioned
to provide not only gigabit access, but also the guar-
anteed quality of service (QoS) to support various time-
sensitive (TS) applications (e.g., cloud virtual reality, onlinegame and industrial automation) [1]. These TS services are
very demanding in system resources on both wireless and
wireline access networks in terms of their capacity and end-to-end (E2E) delay. For wireless access, IEEE 802.11ax-
based wireless local area network (WLAN) is considered as
a key technology for F5G, employing orthogonal frequency
division multiple access (OFDMA) as a new feature to provide
guaranteed QoS [2], [3]. In the wireline segment, passiveoptical networks (PONs) have been widely deployed to pro-
vide broadband access, and are currently evolving towards
ten-gigabit symmetrical PON (XGS-PON) [4]. Since IEEE802.11ax-based WLAN (i.e., Wi-Fi 6) and XGS-PON can both
support 10-Gbit/s data rate, integrating these two networks
with the latter functioning as a backhaul of the former is
considered promising to provide broadband access for F5G [1].
However, in such an integration, how to guarantee the QoSperformance of the integrated network is an important aspect
that needs to be considered.
Extensive efforts are being made to improve the QoS
performance of an integrated PON and Wi-Fi network.

II. I NTEGRATED XGS-PON AND WI-FI6N ETWORK
Figure 1 shows an example of an integrated XGS-PON and
Wi-Fi 6 network, which consists of two segments: wireless
(i.e., Wi-Fi 6) and wireline (i.e., XGS-PON) segments. To con-
nect the two network segments, an access point (AP) in Wi-Fi
6 is connected to an optical network unit (ONU) in XGS-PONvia a standard network interface (e.g., Ethernet). The ONU
is further connected to an optical line terminal (OLT) via an
optical distribution network. Under this conﬁguration, we mayoperate the XGS-PON and the Wi-Fi 6 by themselves and
schedule their network resources independently. Speciﬁcally,
in Wi-Fi 6, with the support of the OFDMA-based random
access (UORA) capability, a station (STA) can quickly access
the wireless network via an AP without requesting pre-reserved resources [4]. However, in this process, collisions
may occur if multiple STAs simultaneously request common
network resources in an uncoordinated manner, which maylead to long access delay for the STA. Moreover, even if the
STA succeeds in forwarding its data to the AP, the latter still
needs to further forward the received data to an associated
ONU and then to an OLT via a shared upstream wavelength in
a time division multiplexing mode, in which the Report/Grant-based DBA mechanism is usually employed to allocate the
bandwidth for the upstream transmission [3]. Here, upon
receiving data from the AP, the ONU needs to report its bufferstatus to the OLT such that the latter can reserve sufﬁcient
bandwidth for the ONU to deliver data in the next transmission
cycle.
In this simple operational mode, resource-reservation infor-
mation is not shared between the two network segments.
Therefore, data transmissions may incur a long delay because
of the following reasons. First, in Wi-Fi 6, collisions in UORA
may lead to a long access delay if an STA cannot obtainnetwork resources quickly (e.g., data 2 in Fig. 1). Second,
the received data in the APs may have to wait for bandwidth
to be transmitted to associated ONUs via standard networkinterfaces, thereby resulting in long queueing delay. Third,
in XGS-PON, the Report/Grant-based DBA mechanism cannot
quickly pre-reserve sufﬁcient bandwidth in the next transmis-
sion cycle although it is possible to predict that there will bea quick data accumulation in the buffer of an ONU in the
next cycle. A long E2E delay may not allow the current inte-
grated network to deliver TS services effectively. Therefore, toshorten the E2E delay so as to allow delivery of TS services
effectively, we propose the CRS scheme introduced next.
III. C
OOPERATIVE RESOURCE SCHEDULING SCHEME
In the proposed CRS scheme, an AP is ﬁrst integrated
with an ONU to form a single physical unit called ONU-AP,
in which the MAC information of AP and ONU can be easilyshared to enable cooperative resource scheduling. Since both
XGS-PON and Wi-Fi 6 schedule their resources in a cyclic
manner, we set the Wi-Fi 6’s scheduling cycle Tto be a
multiple of the XGS-PON’s scheduling cycle τto synchronize
their resource scheduling cyc les. Note that because XGS-PON
has a ﬁxed scheduling cycle and Wi-Fi 6 has a ﬂexible
scheduling cycle, we set the latter to be a multiple of the
former based on the delay requirements of the TS services.In this way, the delay in waiting to forward data from an AP
to its associated ONU can be reduced. On the other hand,
the system spectrum resource in Wi-Fi 6 is allocated based
on time-frequency resource units (RUs), while the resource
in XGS-PON is allocated based on just the time domain.It is important to effectively map the time-frequency RUs in
Wi-Fi 6 to the time slots in XGS-PON to support F5G TS
services well. To further reduce the E2E delay of the TSservices, the CRS maps Wi-Fi 6 and XGS-PON resources
based on their QoS levels, and schedules the two types of
resources in a coordinated manner.

and 20 STA_Ns. In Wi-Fi 6, there are a total of 30 RUsto support the OFDMA-based random access, among which

V. C
ONCLUSION
We proposed a CRS scheme for an integrated XGS-PON
and Wi-Fi 6 network, in which th eir scheduling cycles are syn-
chronized to help reduce the delay of data forwarding betweenONU and AP, and by obtaining the Wi-Fi 6 scheduling
information, the OLT can pre-assign bandwidth to TS services
to reduce the delay caused by PON upstream schedulingand queueing. Simulation results show that, compared with
a benchmark scheme that does not consider the cooperative
effort, the proposed scheme can signiﬁcantly reduce the E2E
delay of TS services up to 50% without sacriﬁcing the
performance of non-TS services.

Behavioural factors affecting HIV prevention among Youths include inadequate knowledge about HIV transmission and prevention methods, misconceptions about the disease, and low condom use during sexual encounters. A study in Nigeria found that more than half of the respondents (53.9%) reported not using a condom in their last sexual encounter (O et al., 2013). Additionally, the willingness to pay for HIV prevention commodities, such as condoms, among key population groups can influence the accessibility and utilization of these commodities (Durosinmi-Etti et al., 2022). 
Furthermore, cultural factors and social stigma surrounding HIV and sexual health discussions can also impact the effectiveness of prevention efforts (Iwelunmor et al., 2014) and limited access to prevention resources. 
To address these factors, it is essential to provide accurate information, promote open discussions, create supportive environments for Youths to make informed decisions about their sexual health and provide adequate infrastructural facilities and trained human resources providing services.
Program outcomes and objectives; Logic model of change 
The program objectives for the proposed school-based program for youths to prevent HIV in Nigeria are to increase knowledge, attitudes, and behaviours related to HIV prevention among Nigerian teens. The program aims to address the knowledge gap and behaviour risks related to HIV among adolescents and young adults in Nigeria (Okudo, 2014) (Chizoba et al., 2020).
The program objectives will be achieved through a combination of evidence-based behaviour change interventions, including peer education, tailored, innovative, and adaptive HIV prevention solutions, and community engagement (Maduakolam et al., 2022) (Chizoba et al., 2020). The program will also promote the uptake of HIV testing and counselling services, as well as the use of HIV self-testing kits Arije et al. (2023).
Overall, the program objectives aim to reduce HIV vulnerability in Nigeria by leveraging evidence-based behaviour change interventions and engaging youth in the design and implementation process. By addressing the unique needs of this population, the program aims to contribute to the ongoing efforts to curb the HIV epidemic in Nigeria and improve the overall health and well-being of adolescents and young adults (Maduakolam et al., 2022) (Chizoba et al., 2020).The program's primary outcome is to reduce the incidence of HIV among Nigerian Youths.

Implementation strategy 
In developing the implementation strategy for the school-based HIV prevention program, we can consider the linkage approach and diffusion theory. The linkage approach emphasizes the importance of building partnerships and collaborations with local stakeholders, including schools, health professionals, and community organizations. This approach will help to help ensure that the program is culturally appropriate, relevant, and sustainable in the long term.
Diffusion theory, on the other hand, would focuse on the spread of innovations and ideas through social networks. Leveraging existing social networks among Nigerian Youths teachers, and peer educators, the program can increase its reach and impact. Peer-led discussions and group activities can help promote positive social norms around HIV prevention and encourage healthy behaviors.
The implementation strategy will involve a phased approach to ensure the program's success and sustainability and will involve the following steps:
Establish partnerships with local stakeholders, including schools, health professionals, and community organizations.
Train teachers and peer educators on the program's content and delivery methods, using the behaviour change matrix and communication methods/practical applications.

Evaluation plan 
The evaluation plan for the school-based HIV prevention program will include both process and effect evaluations. The process evaluation will assess the completeness and fidelity of the program's implementation, including context, reach, dose delivered, dose received, and recruitment. The process evaluation will use both qualitative and quantitative methods, such as surveys, interviews, and focus groups with teachers, peer educators, and students. The frequency of assessment will depend on the specific variable being assessed.
The effect evaluation will focus on the specific behaviour change objectives identified in the behaviour change matrix. The effect evaluation will be determinant/change objective-based, measuring changes in knowledge, attitudes, skills, social norms, and access related to HIV prevention. One limitation of the evaluation plan is the lack of a control group, which may limit the ability to attribute changes in behaviour and health outcomes solely to the program. However, the use of a pre-post design and the inclusion of multiple variables in the process evaluation can help strengthen the evaluation's internal validity.
